Article 1: This law establishes the statute of the
Central Bank of Tunisia.

TITLE ONE
GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 2:
1) The Central Bank of Tunisia, hereinafter referred to as "the central bank," is a public institution
with legal personality and financial autonomy.

2) The central bank is independent in the achievement of its objectives, the exercise of its missions, and
the management of its resources. It is subject to the oversight of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People and is accountable to it regarding the achievement of its objectives and the exercise of its missions in accordance with the provisions of Article 80 of this law.

3) No one may infringe upon the independence of the
central bank, nor influence the decisions of its bodies and its agents in the exercise of their functions.

Article 3: The central bank is deemed to be a merchant
in its dealings with third parties to the extent that this is not derogated from by laws and its own statute. The provisions of the public accounting code are not applicable to it.

The staff of the Central Bank are subject to a special statute approved by government decree.
Said statute provides for at least the fundamental rights and guarantees provided for by law n° 78-85 of August 5, 1985, concerning the general statute of agents of offices, public industrial and commercial establishments, and companies whose capital belongs directly and entirely to the State or local authorities.
Said special statute guarantees the possibility of secondment and integration of executives from the public sector to the central bank. TITLE II
OBJECTIVES AND MISSIONS OF THE CENTRAL BANK

Article 7: The primary objective of the central bank is to maintain price stability.
The central bank contributes to maintaining financial stability in a way that supports the achievement of the State's economic policy objectives, including in the areas of development and employment. It works for optimal coordination between monetary policy and the State's economic policy.

Article 8: The central bank is notably responsible for:
- conducting and implementing monetary policy,
- applying laws and regulations relating to foreign exchange,
- holding and managing foreign exchange reserves in foreign currencies and gold.
- working to ensure the stability, efficiency, and security of payment systems, while taking into account the specificities of Islamic finance,
- supervising banks and financial institutions and regulating banking activity,
- issuing and ensuring the maintenance of fiduciary currency and facilitating its circulation in Tunisia,
- acting as the State's cashier and financial agent,
- acting as the government's financial advisor and issuing an opinion on economic and financial matters when requested,
- collecting and managing all data related to the exercise of its missions,
- contributing to the conduct and implementation of macroprudential policy with a view to preventing and mitigating systemic risk,
- working to protect users of banking services.

Article 9: For the exercise of its missions, the Central Bank may notably undertake the following operations:

1) Open cash and securities accounts on its books, regardless of the currency, for the benefit of the State, banks, public enterprises and establishments, financial institutions, foreign banks Article 12: Any refinancing operation of a debt by the central bank automatically results in the subrogation of the central bank in the rights and obligations that the beneficiary of the refinancing has against their own debtor.

CHAPTER II
EMISSION PRIVILEGE

Article 13: The central bank, on behalf of the State, exercises the exclusive privilege of issuing banknotes and coins in Tunisia.

Article 14:
1°) Only banknotes and coins issued by the central bank have legal tender, to the exclusion of all other banknotes and coins.
2°) Banknotes issued by the Central Bank have unlimited purchasing power.
3°) The purchasing power of coins issued by the Central Bank is fixed by law. They are accepted without limitation by the central bank and by public treasuries.

Article 15:
1°) The creation and issuance of banknotes and coins by the central bank, as well as their withdrawal or exchange, are carried out under the conditions determined by Article 64 of this law.
2°) No opposition can be served upon the central bank concerning the loss or theft of banknotes.
3°) The reimbursement of a mutilated or damaged banknote is granted when the banknote bears sufficient identifying marks and signs. In other cases, full or partial reimbursement is at the discretion of the Central Bank.
4°) The reimbursement of a coin whose identification has become impossible or which has been subject to any alteration or mutilation is granted only if it is proven, to the satisfaction of the Central Bank, that the mutilations or alterations in question are the result of an accident or an act of force majeure.
5°) In case of withdrawal from circulation of one or more categories of banknotes or of 2°) Subject to the provisions of the legislation relating to the protection of personal data, the Central Bank may request information useful for the exercise of its duties provided for in the preceding paragraph from entities operating in the private sector and public sector organizations, even if these entities and organizations are not subject to its control, and this, notwithstanding the obligations incumbent upon them under professional secrecy.
3°) The Central Bank may conclude cooperation agreements with foreign authorities responsible for macroprudential supervision and exchange secret information with them, provided that this information is, according to the applicable laws abroad, covered by professional secrecy and that it is necessary for the accomplishment of the missions of the foreign authorities. The foreign authority must undertake not to communicate this information to third parties without the explicit agreement of the Central Bank and to use it only within the framework of the exercise of its powers.

Article 19:
1) In order to preserve the stability of the financial system, the Central Bank may grant financial assistance in the form of operations referred to in Article 10 of this law to solvent banks and financial institutions whose liquidity is temporarily affected.

2) The Central Bank may grant financial assistance to banks and financial institutions whose solvency is compromised and if their failure presents a threat to the stability of the financial system. The granting of this assistance requires obtaining the guarantee of the State in accordance with the legislation in force.

3) The Central Bank may, where applicable, grant financial assistance to the deposit guarantee fund after obtaining the guarantee of the State in accordance with the legislation in force. This prohibition is not applicable to financial assistance operations granted by the central bank, under the conditions provided for by this law, to banks and financial institutions in which the State directly or indirectly holds a stake.
Article 26: The central bank may, at the request of the minister in charge of finance, provide financial services to administrations, public enterprises and establishments, and all financial organizations governed by special legislative provisions or placed under the supervision of the State as defined by current texts. It may carry out for their benefit all cash, banking, and credit operations in accordance with the conditions fixed by agreements concluded with the aforementioned administrations, public enterprises and establishments, and organizations.
Article 27: The central bank assists the government in its relations with international financial institutions. The governor or their authorized representative for this purpose may, under government delegation, represent the State to the aforementioned institutions or at international congresses.
Article 28:
1°) The central bank participates in negotiations concerning the conclusion of payment or compensation agreements. It may be entrusted with their execution as well as the conclusion of all necessary implementing conventions for this purpose.
2°) The aforementioned agreements are executed on behalf of the State. The State benefits from profits and bears losses, expenses, commissions, interest, and charges related to the execution of these agreements, whatever their nature.
The State guarantees the central bank coverage of any loss arising from exchange rates or any other loss arising directly from the execution of the aforementioned agreements.

Article 33: The central bank may, in its own name and for its own account, lend and borrow in foreign currencies within the limits of its necessary needs.

Article 34:
1°) The central bank may accept, in accounts opened with the approval of its Board of Directors, sums deposited by banks, and by individuals and legal entities.

2°) The central bank shall settle drafts on the said accounts and commitments made at its counters within the limits of available balances.

TITLE III
GOVERNANCE AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE

Article 45: The governance and administration of the central bank are carried out in the following order by: a governor and a board of directors referred to hereinafter as the "board."

CHAPTER ONE
GOVERNOR OF THE CENTRAL BANK

Article 46: The governor of the central bank is appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 78 of the constitution for a term of six years, renewable once. He is chosen from among individuals recognized for their competence in economic, monetary, and financial fields.
The functions of the governor may be terminated before the end of the term mentioned in the first paragraph of this article, in accordance with the provisions of Article 78 of the constitution.

Article 47: The governor shall swear, before the President of the Republic and before taking up his duties, the following oath:
"I swear by Almighty God to direct, with loyalty and fidelity, the affairs of the Central Bank of Tunisia and to fulfill my duties with complete impartiality and independence."

Article 48: Subject to the powers of the board, the governor ensures the management of the Central Bank. To this end, he:
1°) represents the central bank to public authorities, foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and, in general, to third parties,
2°) ensures the application of laws relating to the Central Bank and the deliberations of the board,
3°) implements the monetary policy of the Central Bank as defined by the board, **Article 54**: The governor, the vice-governor, and the secretary-general are prohibited from combining their duties with those of a member of the people's representative assembly or the government, or from assuming partisan responsibility at the central, regional, or local level, or from combining their duties with any function in the public or private sector.

**Article 55**:
1. The remuneration and benefits of the governor, the vice-governor, and the secretary-general shall be fixed by the council. They shall be borne by the central bank.
2. In the event of the cessation of their duties, the governor and the vice-governor shall continue to receive their remuneration for one year.
3. If a public office is entrusted to them during this period, a decision by the head of government shall specify the conditions under which the emoluments inherent to the said office are combined with the aforementioned remuneration.
4. During the same period, they are prohibited from providing services to private companies and receiving compensation for advice or services rendered, except with the authorization of the head of government. In such a case, they shall be deprived of the remuneration provided for in the second paragraph of this article.
5. The council shall determine the conditions under which the governor benefits from representation allowance as well as the conditions for reimbursement of his exceptional expenses.

**Article 56**:
1. During the period of their mandate, the governor and the vice-governor are prohibited from holding any shareholding or having interests in a private company.
2. No commitment signed by the governor or the vice-governor may be admitted into the portfolio of the Central Bank.

Article 1: The purpose of this law is to organize the conditions for carrying out banking operations and the modalities for supervising banks and financial institutions, with a view to preserving their solidity and protecting depositors and users of banking services, in order to contribute to the proper functioning of the banking sector and to achieve financial stability.

Article 2: The provisions of this law apply to banks and financial institutions carrying out their activity in Tunisia, including non-resident banks and financial institutions within the meaning of exchange legislation.
The provisions of the code for the provision of financial services to non-residents, enacted by Law n°2009-64 of August 12, 2009, apply to non-resident banks and financial institutions as long as they are not derogated from by the provisions of this law.
Banks and financial institutions are subject to the provisions of the Commercial Companies Code as long as they are not derogated from by the provisions of this law.

Article 3: The provisions of this law do not apply to entities that carry out banking operations under the laws governing them. They also do not apply to international financial institutions, their representations, or financial cooperation agencies created under agreements concluded with the government of the Tunisian Republic.

Article 17: Any legal person who habitually carries out the collection of deposits within the meaning of Article 5 of this law and provides the customer base with means of payment, with a view to carrying out the other banking operations referred to in Article 4 of this law, is considered a bank.
Each bank licensed in accordance with the provisions of this law qualifies as a licensed intermediary for carrying out foreign exchange operations within the meaning of the legislation in force concerning foreign exchange.

Article 18: Any legal person who habitually carries out the banking operations referred to in the provisions of the first chapter of this title, with the exception of collecting public deposits and providing the customer base with means of payment, is considered a financial institution.

Article 19: Any financial institution that habitually carries out the following operations as a specialized activity is considered an investment bank:

- Taking participations within the framework of restructuring operations, involving an undertaking to resell within a period not exceeding five years.
The resources of investment banks exclusively comprise their own funds and borrowed resources.
Investment banks licensed in accordance with this law may use the term "bank" in their company name and in all their documents and advertising, provided that the term "investment bank" is added in all cases.

**Article 43:** Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a policy aimed at the effective management of conflicts of interest.

To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia shall establish rules governing operations with persons having ties to the bank or financial institution, within the meaning of this law, and in particular the limits on financing granted.

A person having ties to the bank or financial institution is considered to be:

*   any shareholder whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the capital of the bank or financial institution,
*   any spouse, ascendant, and descendant of a natural person whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the capital of the bank or financial institution,
*   any company in which the bank or financial institution holds a stake in the capital such that it leads to its control or decisive influence over its activities,
*   the chairman of the board of directors of a bank or financial institution, the general director, the members of the board of directors, the deputy general directors, the members of the supervisory board, the members of the executive board, the members of the banking standards compliance control committee. A person is considered an independent member within the meaning of this law if they have no links with the said bank or the said institution, or with its shareholders or its directors, of a nature that could compromise the independence of their decisions or lead them into a situation of actual or potential conflict of interest.

Small shareholders are considered to be the public within the meaning of the legislation governing the financial market.

The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the criteria determining the quality of independence.

Article 48: The board of directors or the supervisory board defines the strategy of the bank or financial institution and ensures its execution is monitored. The board of directors or the supervisory board is notably responsible for:

*   Monitoring the degree of commitment of the bank's or financial institution's management in implementing the governance framework and periodically evaluating this framework for its adaptation to significant changes in the bank or financial institution, particularly in terms of business size, operational complexity, market evolution, and organizational requirements.
*   Establishing, in consultation with the general management or the executive board, a risk appetite strategy that takes into account the competitive and regulatory environment as well as the bank's or financial institution's capacity to control risks.
*   Appointing the general management or the executive board.
*   Closing the financial statements and preparing the annual report of the bank or financial institution. **Article 50:** The bank or financial institution must create a Risk Committee, stemming from the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, which assists it in particular in establishing a risk management strategy and which will be responsible, in particular:

- for periodically evaluating the risk management policy and its implementation,
- for monitoring the activity of the body responsible for risk management.

**Article 51:** Every bank must create a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, stemming from the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, which assists it in particular in the design and monitoring of policies for:
- nomination and remuneration,

Article 149: Pursuant to this law, a fund called "the bank deposit guarantee fund" is hereby established, aiming to protect depositors and compensate them in the event of the unavailability of their deposits within the meaning of Article 153 of this law. In order to contribute to financial stability, the fund may grant financing to a member bank in a compromised situation within the framework of the resolution plan provided for by Title VII of this law, in the following forms:
- repayable secured loans,
- equity stakes in the bank's capital.
The bank deposit guarantee fund may take stakes in the bridge institution provided for by Article 117 of this law.
The guarantee fund may mobilize borrowed resources.

Article 150: Every bank licensed within the meaning of this law must adhere to the bank deposit guarantee fund.
The bank deposit guarantee fund shall be responsible for the collection and management of bank contributions.
The fund shall take into consideration the specificities of banks that exclusively conduct Islamic banking operations and non-resident banks within the meaning of Article 2 of this law, by allocating a special account to each category of bank.
The fund must take the necessary internal measures to ensure compliance **Article 152:** The deposit guarantee fund compensates depositors within a determined ceiling.
The ceiling, terms, and compensation procedures shall be set by governmental decree.
For the purpose of depositor compensation, the global account provided for in Article 21 of this law, opened by payment institutions with the bank, shall not be considered a single account. The nominative list accompanying the payment accounts opened with the payment institution shall be used as a reference.
The following deposits are excluded from the guarantee of the deposit guarantee fund:
- From the State, public enterprises, and establishments,
- From the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- From banks, financial institutions, and their subsidiaries,
- From the Tunisian Post, insurance and reinsurance companies,
- From collective investment undertakings, stockbrokers, and investment companies,
- From members of the board of directors, supervisory board, executive board, chief executive officer, and deputy chief executive officers of the bank concerned by the compensation of its deposits,
- From any shareholder holding a stake of 5% or more in the capital of the bank provided for in Article 32 of this law and deposits from companies under their control,
- From the auditors of the bank,
- From the spouse, ascendants, and descendants of the natural persons referred to in points 6, 7, and 8 of this article,
- From funds placed with the bank concerned by the compensation in the form of money market financial instruments.

**Article 153:** The Central Bank of Tunisia shall ascertain the unavailability of the funds mentioned in Article 149 of this law when it appears to it that a bank is no longer, due to its financial situation, able to repay immediately or in the short term the deposits it has received. Article 156: The supervisory committee of the bank deposit guarantee fund comprises the following five members:
- two members independent of shareholders and members, appointed by governmental decree, one of whom holds the position of chairman,
- a representative of the Central Bank of Tunisia with the rank of Director General, member,
- a representative of the ministry responsible for finance with the rank of Director General, member,
- a third-grade judge, member.
The members of the supervisory committee referred to in points 2, 3, and 4 of this article are appointed by governmental decree upon the proposal of the Central Bank of Tunisia, the minister responsible for finance, and with the concurring opinion of the Superior Council of the Magistracy, each as far as they are concerned.

The members of the supervisory committee are appointed for a term of three years, renewable only once.

Article 157: Within the bank deposit guarantee fund, a committee named the "Audit and Risk Committee" is established, stemming from the supervisory committee and responsible, in particular, for:
- assisting the supervisory committee in the design and implementation of an internal control system,
- examining the annual activity report and the financial statements of the fund before their transmission to the supervisory committee,
- supervising the activities of the internal audit department and, where applicable, supervising and coordinating the work of other departments responsible for control missions,
- proposing a strategy and policy for risk management,
- evaluating the results of investments made and the risk coverage policy.

The Audit and Risk Committee transmits a detailed report on its activities to the supervisory committee.
The composition of the committee and the rules for its operation and the remuneration of its members are determined by a decision of the supervisory committee.

Article 158: The **Article 160:** The accounts of the bank deposit guarantee fund shall be subject to an annual audit conducted by two auditors registered on the list of the Order of Chartered Accountants of Tunisia, appointed by the supervisory committee for a term of three years, renewable only once, based on a call for applications. Notwithstanding their legal obligations, the auditors are required to submit their report on the fund's financial statements to the supervisory committee within three months of the closing of the accounting year. The fund's accounting shall be kept in accordance with the enterprise accounting system.

**Article 161:** The supervisory committee shall transmit the annual activity report of the bank deposit guarantee fund and a copy of the auditors' report to the ministry in charge of finance and the Central Bank of Tunisia. The fund shall publish its financial statements in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic and in two daily newspapers, one of which shall be in Arabic.

**Article 162:** The Central Bank of Tunisia and the ministry in charge of finance may appoint a committee composed of their representatives with a view to undertaking an audit mission of the fund.

**Article 163:** The bank deposit guarantee fund shall be subject to oversight by the Court of Accounts at least once every 3 years.

ON SANCTIONS
CHAPTER ONE
ON DISCIPLINARY SANCTIONS

Article 169: The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia is empowered to impose the sanctions provided for in Article 170 of this law against banks and financial institutions that commit one of the following offenses:
- Non-compliance with prudential, governance, and internal control standards provided for by this law and by the regulatory provisions issued by the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to obtain authorizations and the obligation to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia, particularly concerning appointments, outsourcing, products, banking conditions, establishment inside and outside the country, including the opening and closing of branches, subsidiaries, or periodic offices,
- Non-compliance with legal and regulatory provisions relating to the facilitation of supervision procedures for banks and financial institutions, including responding to requests related to information and data necessary for the Central Bank of Tunisia to exercise its supervisory functions,
- Non-compliance with regulatory provisions concerning internal control rules related to the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to notify operations provided for in Article 37 of this law,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to pay the annual amount provided for in Article 73 of this law.

Article 170: The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia shall pronounce one of the following two sanctions in respect of the offenses provided for in Article 169 of this law:
1- A warning,
2- A fine whose amount shall not exceed 15% of the minimum capital of the bank or of the category of the financial institution in question. Members of the sanctions commission are appointed by government decree for a term of 3 years, renewable once.

The commission holds its meetings at the headquarters of the Central Bank of Tunisia. The general directorate responsible for banking supervision provides its secretariat.
The commission's decisions must be reasoned and are taken by a majority of votes.

The commission establishes its internal regulations, which are approved by government decree.

Members of the sanctions commission are bound by professional secrecy regarding information they become aware of in the performance of their duties. They must refrain from using this information, outside of cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required for the execution of their assigned missions. This obligation continues even after they lose their status, under penalty of facing the sanctions provided for in Article 254 of the penal code.

Article 172: The sanctions commission shall impose one of the sanctions provided for in Article 173 of the present law against banks and financial institutions that commit any of the following offenses:
- Carrying out banking operations without respecting the category, specialty, or conditions provided for by their license,
- Violation of legal and regulatory provisions concerning transactions with persons connected to banks or financial institutions,
- Obtaining a license by a bank or financial institution through false declarations,
- Refusal to comply with the instructions of the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Intentional concealment of information or voluntary communication of inaccurate information,
- Intentional obstruction of the missions of banking supervision to be carried out by agents of the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Refusal to pay the annual contribution to the bank deposit guarantee fund.
Artic The bank, financial institution, or the concerned person may be assisted by a lawyer, concerning offenses within the competence of the sanctions commission.

Article 177: The bank, financial institution, or the concerned person shall be informed of the facts of which they are accused by any means leaving a written record.
The legal representative of the bank, financial institution, or the concerned person or their representative has the right to consult the file of the offenses being prosecuted at the headquarters of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
The legal representative of the bank, financial institution, or the concerned person must send their written observations to the Central Bank of Tunisia or to the sanctions commission within a period of eight days from the date of receipt of the notification provided for in the first paragraph of this article.

Article 178: The sanctions commission is responsible for the investigation of files of offenses within its competence, upon referral by the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
It shall rule on the aforementioned offenses, in accordance with the procedures provided for by this law.

Article 179: Sanctions shall be imposed by the sanctions commission and by the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia, each in their respective capacities, and shall be communicated to the bank, financial institution in question, or the concerned person by any means leaving a written record.

Article 180: Decisions rendered under Article 179 of this law shall be included in the annual banking supervision reports issued by the Central Bank of Tunisia and published on its website.

Article 181: Any delay or refusal to communicate the documents, information, clarifications, and justifications referred to in Article 71 of this law shall be subject to a penalty. TITLE X

Article 186: Banks and financial institutions are required to establish a professional association, with the objective of working to study issues related to the practice of the profession and its development, as well as human resource training. The association also plays the role of an intermediary between its members, on the one hand, and the public authorities and the Central Bank of Tunisia, on the other, for any matter concerning the profession. The minister responsible for finance and the governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may consult the association on any matter relating to the evolution of the profession, and the association may submit proposals to this effect. The association must establish a code of ethics that is binding on its members and work to ensure its compliance.

Article 187: The association referred to in Article 186 of this law must create a banking mediation body responsible for examining requests submitted to it by clients concerning their disputes with banks and financial institutions. Each bank or financial institution may, for the same purposes, appoint one or more banking mediators. The banking mediation body or the banking mediator shall be seized of requests submitted to them, free of charge and within a maximum period of eight days from the receipt of the mediation request. It may not consider requests for which arbitration or settlement is not permitted or which are the subject of cases pending before the courts. 4.1. The operations provided for in Article 24 of Law No. 2016-48 require an approval in principle and a final approval from the Approval Commission, in accordance with the provisions of Article 30 of the said law.

4.2. The approval in principle defines, in particular, the category of the establishment, the nature of the authorized operations, the initial capital, as well as the identity of the reference shareholder and the principal shareholders, and sets the requirements and conditions necessary to be met for the granting of final approval, in accordance with the provisions of Article 30 of Law No. 2016-48.

4.3. The applicant for approval must satisfy the conditions defined by the final approval within a period not exceeding six months from the date of notification of the approval in principle. This period may be exceptionally extended for a duration of 3 months, based on a duly reasoned request from the applicant.

4.4. The approval in principle shall be withdrawn by the Approval Commission if the applicant has not satisfied the required conditions within the six-month period from the date of notification of the approval decision. This shall be based on a reasoned report from the Central Bank of Tunisia indicating the non-compliance with the conditions required at the time of granting the approval in principle.

4.5. Final approval shall be granted by the Approval Commission upon a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia within a period of two months from the receipt of a request from the applicant proving compliance with all the conditions required and defined in the approval in principle, in particular:

- The completion of the incorporation procedures:

**Article 50:** Banking services and investment services, as defined by the following articles of this title, are considered financial services within the meaning of this Code.

**Article 51:** Banking services include:
1. The reception of deposits from non-residents, regardless of their duration and form;
2. The granting of credit to non-residents in all its forms;
3. The provision to resident clients and the management of payment instruments;
4. Foreign exchange operations with non-residents and, within the limits authorized by current legislation and regulations, with residents.

The definitions provided by Articles 3, 4, and 5 of Law No. 2001-65 of July 10, 2001, relating to credit institutions, apply to deposits, credits, and payment instruments.

**Article 52:** Services related to banking services include:
1. Advice and assistance in investment and wealth management, financial management and engineering, and generally all services intended to facilitate the creation, development, and restructuring of businesses; and

**Article 1:** Authorized intermediary banks may, in accordance with current legislation, carry out manual currency exchange activity within specialized agencies called "exchange bureaus."

**Article 1:** The premises of the exchange office must be visible and identifiable to the public.

**Article 2:** Approved intermediary banks must take all necessary security measures relating to the protection of persons and the premises of the exchange office.

They must ensure that the premises are permanently connected to the police station by means of a special telephone line.

**Article 3:** Approved intermediary banks must have a procedures manual relating to the security of the exchange office premises, notably describing police alert procedures in the event of justified concerns or aggression. **SUBJECT: Activity of Non-Resident Banks.**

Law n°85-108 of December 6, 1985, encouraging financial and banking institutions working essentially with non-residents, has broadened the scope of activity of these institutions by allowing them, among other things, to now conduct banking activities with residents under the conditions it determines. It has simultaneously placed upon them the obligation to ensure, in the exercise of their functions, the preservation of the credit of the Tunis Place by conforming, in particular, to international rules and practices.

The purpose of this circular is to specify the financial management conditions of these institutions and the rules governing their activity with residents. It also provides some clarifications regarding the roles these institutions perform in their capacity as Authorized Intermediaries, concerning the exchange control regime, as well as banking conditions and ratios applicable to them.

**I - GENERAL FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT CONDITIONS**

For the guarantee of their solvency and liquidity, non-resident banks are obligated to ensure, concerning:

*   **Adjustment of their resources and uses:** that their financial situation allows them to meet their commitments at all times.
*   **Their exchange risks:** that their exchange positions conform to generally accepted international security standards.

**II - SPECIFIC RULES FOR ACTIVITY WITH RESIDENTS:**

**1°) Collection and Use of Funds in Dinars:**

**a) Collection of Funds from Residents:**
Law n°85-108 of December 6, 1985, authorizes non-resident banks to collect funds from residents, provided that the total of these funds does not exceed, for each institution... b) Financing of foreign trade operations:

Article 8, paragraph 4 of Law No. 85-108 of December 6, 1985, authorizes non-resident banks to finance import and export operations with foreign currency resources. Within this framework, they can grant their support to residents.

- Financing of imports:

The financing of imports can be carried out regardless of the regulation of the products to be imported (prohibited, subject to quotas, liberalized). The financial settlement of imports must be handled by the non-resident bank.

Disbursements are made at the earliest on the date on which the foreign exchange regulation, following the procedure, allows the transfer to be made.

- Financing of exports:

The financing of exports can be carried out regardless of the regulation of the products to be exported (prohibited, subject to quotas, liberalized). It is carried out within the limit of the amount provided for in the commercial contract, at the earliest from the date of customs declaration of the export document.

Financing can be carried out in any convertible foreign currency, regardless of the currency of the commercial contract.

The amount of financing granted by the bank must be immediately and entirely transferred, for the account of the beneficiary, to the Central Bank of Tunisia. This operation cannot result in an entry in the "Exportations Frais Accessoires" (EFAC) or "Voyage d'Affaires" accounts until the repatriation of export proceeds.

III - CONDITIONS FOR EXERCISING THE ROLE OF AUTHORIZED INTERMEDIARY:

Non-resident banks can carry out related foreign trade operations for the account of the clients they finance, such as the domiciliation of foreign trade instruments, the opening of documentary credits, and Exportations and Frais Accessoires accounts. 2°) Operations in Dinars:
Regarding income earned by non-resident banks from operations carried out with residents and financed from their dinar resources in accordance with the provisions of Article 8, paragraph 5 of Law n°85-108, such income may be transferred with the authorization of the Central Bank of Tunisia. The request for authorization must be accompanied by the balance sheet and the income statement pertaining to the financial year to which the said income relates.

3°) Regularity of Operations:
In accordance with Article 22 of Law n°85-108 of December 6, 1985, non-resident banks are required to ensure the regularity of operations to be carried out with residents, and in this regard, they are responsible for any violation of current legislation and regulations.

V- BANK CONDITIONS:
1°) Operations in Dinars:
The debit and credit conditions and the commissions that non-resident banks are authorized to apply to dinar operations with their resident clientele are those provided for in this matter by the circulars of the Central Bank of Tunisia to resident banks, and in particular circulars n°85-15 of April 15, 1985, 79-41 of December 4, 1979, and 85-25 and 85-26 of July 2, 1985.

Non-resident banks must request authorization from the Central Bank of Tunisia for the conditions they propose to apply to forms of resources or uses not covered by these circulars.

2°) Foreign Exchange Operations:
Non-resident banks may grant foreign exchange credits to residents under the following conditions:

- Short-term credits: The lending rate must be that of the international market representative of the contract currency, increased by a maximum margin of 3/8 of one percent.

Non-resident banks authorized to collect funds in dinars are subject to the mandatory reserve under the same conditions as resident deposit banks.

3°) Public Securities Ratio:

Non-resident banks authorized to collect funds in dinars are subject to the public securities ratio, the details of which will be specified later.

VII - ACCOUNTING ORGANIZATION AND PERIODIC DECLARATIONS TO THE CENTRAL BANK OF TUNISIA:

1°) Accounting Organization:

Non-resident banks, being authorized to carry out operations with residents, concurrently with their main activity with non-residents, and applying to each of the two categories of operations their specific exchange rules, must individualize their accounting for operations with residents.

Article 1: Leasing is an operation of the rental
of equipment, machinery, or real estate
purchased or manufactured for the purpose of rental, by the lessor
who remains the owner and intended for use in
professional, commercial, industrial,
agricultural, fishing, or service activities.

Leasing is carried out by a written contract, for
a determined duration, in exchange for rent and allows
the lessee the acquisition, at the end of the rental period,
of all or part of the equipment, machinery, or
real estate, for an agreed price which takes into account,
at least in part, the payments made
as rent.

The lessee may, with the agreement of the lessor, acquire
during the rental period, all or part of the said
equipment, machinery, or real estate.

Article 2: The leasing contract is governed by the
provisions of common law to the extent that they are not
derogated from by this law.

All clauses and stipulations and all arrangements contrary to
the provisions of Article 1 of this law are null and void.

Article 3: The provisions of law n°77 -37 of May 25, 1977, governing relations between lessors and lessees
with regard to the renewal of leases
of buildings or premises for commercial, industrial, or artisanal use, are not applicable to leasing contracts.
The leasing contract must regulate the relations between the
lessor and the lessee, particularly regarding
rents and the conditions for its termination at the request of the lessee.

The lessor may not rely, to assert their rights, on a contract that does not provide for clauses
relating to rent and the conditions for its termination at the request of the lessee.

Decides:

Article 1: The purpose of this circular is to set out the conditions for the application of articles 20 and 21 of law n°2016 -48 on banks and financial institutions.
It defines, in particular, Payment services must be provided exclusively in Tunisian Dinars and within the territory of the Republic of Tunisia.
To this end, payment institutions shall directly adhere to the payment and clearing systems appropriate to their activity.

Article 3: In accordance with the provisions of paragraph 5 of Article 21 of the aforementioned Law No. 2016-48, payment institutions must contract professional civil liability insurance or a bank guarantee of a sufficient amount, commensurate with their own funds, to cover their liability when providing payment services.

The minimum amount of the insurance policy or bank guarantee must be determined by the payment institutions based on the following criteria:
- The risk profile of the institution,
- The type of activity and payment services provided by the institution, and
- The volume of the institution's activity.

Payment institutions must implement a methodological approach for calculating the insurance policy or bank guarantee and submit this approach for the prior approval of the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Payment institutions are required to review, once a year, and, if necessary, modify the minimum amount of their insurance policy or guarantee.

Article 4: Payment institutions may carry out operations involving the reception of funds from abroad by wire transfer, and make them available to their clients after obtaining the status of an authorized intermediary in accordance with the foreign exchange regulations in force.

Governance Rules

- Assisting the administrative body in the design and implementation of an internal control system;
- Examining the annual report on the management of the institution and the financial statements before their approval by the administrative body;
- Monitoring the activities of the structures responsible for internal audit and risk; and
- Proposing a risk management policy adapted to the nature of the payment activity and monitoring its implementation.

Article 8: Payment institutions are subject to the provisions of Circular No. 2006-1 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of November 28, 2006, relating to internal control. To this end, they must implement an internal control system adapted to the nature, size, and complexity of their activities and the risks associated with them.

Article 9: Payment institutions must be equipped with:
- An information system that is commensurate with the nature and complexity of payment operations;
- An operational security system that ensures perfect traceability of executed payment operations and collected funds, allows for the identification of performed operations, provides the position of all open payment accounts, and prevents the risk of intrusion and risks related to fraud through organizational measures and prevention tools;
- A system for recording and processing payment operations in real-time, both at the level of the payment institutions themselves and at the level of their payment agent networks defined by Title IV of this circular;
- A system for processing and protecting the personal data of their clients in accordance with legal provisions. Without prejudice to the provisions of the first paragraph of this article, payment institutions are required to apply the customer identification rules provided for in Article 14 of this circular.

**Article 12**: Payment institutions must keep records of payment transactions, which must be retained for a period of at least 10 years from the execution of said transactions.

**Article 13**: Payment institutions are subject to specific and regular reporting, the terms of which are set by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

**Title III**: Rules for opening and operating payment accounts and the global account

**Article 14**: Payment institutions are authorized to open three levels of payment accounts: "Level 1 account," "Level 2 account," and "Level 3 account."

Each level of payment account must correspond to:
* Limits for the balance ceiling and the total amount of fund outflows from the payment account per day.
* Customer identification rules as defined in this circular.

The aforementioned limits and rules are set as follows:

* **Level 1 Payment Account**: The balance of this account is capped at 500 dinars, without the total amount of fund outflows from the payment account exceeding 250 dinars per day. The opening of this account requires the customer to have a national mobile phone number and a copy of an official identity document of said customer, valid and bearing their photograph, issued by an authorized Tunisian authority or a recognized foreign authority.

* **Level 2 Payment Account**: The balance of this account is capped at 1000 dinars, without the total amount of fund outflows from the payment account exceeding 500 dinars per day. **On the use of payment agent networks**

**Article 24:** Payment institutions may, under their responsibility and on their own behalf, and subject to the restrictions provided for in this circular, mandate legal entities or natural persons who are merchants, in order to offer payment services.

**Article 25:** Payment institutions must establish a policy for the use of payment agents that covers, in particular, the selection, training, control, and profile of these agents (natural or legal persons, their targeted business sectors, and their geographical locations…).

**Article 26:** Payment institutions are required to notify the Central Bank of Tunisia of any planned mandate to be concluded with a payment agent.

**Article 27:** Payment institutions may mandate two categories of payment agents:
a- **Principal payment agents** who may only provide the following services:
    * the opening of Level 1 and Level 2 payment accounts as defined by Article 14 of this circular;
    * cash payment operations;
    * cash deposits and withdrawals on a payment account; and
    * fund transfer operations.

b- **Retail payment agents** who may only provide the following services:
    * the opening of Level 1 payment accounts as defined by Article 14 of this circular;
    * cash deposits and withdrawals on a payment account; and
    * cash payment operations.

Payment institutions cannot mandate payment agents for the remote opening of payment accounts.

**Article 28:** Principal payment agents and retail payment agents may offer payment services for the account of one or more payment institutions.

**Article 29:** Before entering into **Article 30:** The payment institution must conclude an agreement with its principal agents and its retail agents that specifies, at a minimum:
- the payment services offered by the payment agents;
- the legal and financial responsibility of the payment agents;
- the obligations of the payment institution towards the payment agents regarding training, implementation of procedures, documents, support, and technical means necessary for the provision of payment services for which they are mandated;
- the methods of control carried out by the payment institution on the payment agents;
- the remuneration arrangements for services offered by the payment agents on behalf of the payment institution, and
- the prohibition for a principal payment agent or a retail payment agent to delegate or transfer their mandate to another payment agent or any other person.

**Article 31:** The payment institution may only mandate payment agents who open a "payment agent account" on its books, which operates according to the following rules:
- the payment agent account must be intended for the exclusive execution of the payment services listed in Article 27 of this circular only;
- credit facilities granted by the payment institution on the payment agent account are prohibited, and
- the payment agent account may not at any time show a debit balance.

The payment institution shall take the necessary measures to ensure that the payment services listed in Article 27 of this circular are executed only within the limit of the available credit balance on the payment agent account.

The ceiling rules listed in Article 14 of this circular do not apply to the payment agent account.

to banks and financial institutions.

Article 2: For the purposes of this circular, Islamic banking operations take the form
either of commercial financing operations, or of participatory financing operations, or of investment
deposits.

Title One: Commercial Financing Operations
Article 3: Commercial financing operations include Mourabaha, Ijara,
Istisna'a and Salam.

Article 4: Financing by "Mourabaha" is an operation whereby the bank or
financial institution, following a request from the client who placed the order, acquires movable or immovable
assets or services from a third party and resells them to the client who placed the order at a price equivalent to their acquisition cost plus a profit margin determined in advance, in the form
of a fixed amount or a fixed percentage of the initial acquisition value. **Article 5:** Mourabaha financing is granted to:
1- Professionals in the form of:
    - Pre-financing of operations for the acquisition of raw materials, finished products, or semi-finished products necessary for production or trade;
    - Financing the acquisition of assets, rights, or services, within the framework of investment projects carried out by individuals or legal entities in all economic sectors.
2- Individuals to finance:
    - The acquisition, construction, or extension of real estate;
    - The acquisition of movable property;
    - The acquisition of services.

**Article 6:** "Ijara" financing for professionals is considered an operation by which the bank or financial institution acquires an asset, takes ownership of it, and then leases it to the client, granting them the option to purchase it.

**Article 7:** "Salam" financing is an operation by which the bank or financial institution carries out a forward purchase at a cash price of determined tangible movable goods specified by the client.
The bank or financial institution is obliged to sell the movable goods subject to the "Salam" after their reception, or to mandate the client for this purpose, within the established deadlines.
The bank or financial institution may sell the goods subject to the "Salam" before their reception within the framework of a second "Salam" for the benefit of a third party.

**Article 8:** "Istisna'a" financing is an operation by which the bank or financial institution finances the manufacturing of a movable or immovable good for its client, acting as the "Mostasni'i," according to determined specifications.
To this end, the bank or financial institution:
- Commissions a third party, known as the "Sani'i," to manufacture the asset requested **Title II: Participatory Financing Operations**

**Article 9:** Participatory financing operations include, in particular, financing by "Moucharaka" and financing by "Moudharaba."

**Article 10:** Financing by "Moucharaka" is an operation whereby the bank or financial institution co-finances, with its client, according to agreed proportions and duration, the cost of carrying out a project, an activity, or specific commercial operations.

**Article 11:** Financing by "Moudharaba" is an operation whereby the bank or financial institution provides the entirety of the capital to the client for the purpose of financing a project or an activity. The client's contribution is limited to expertise and management.

**Title III: Investment Deposits**

**Article 12:** Investment deposits are considered to be amounts lodged by their holders, by any means of payment whatsoever, in an investment account opened with a bank, for the purpose of investing them, under a contract of "Moudharaba" or "Wakala investment," in assets for a determined period, with or without restrictions.

"Wakala investment" is an operation whereby the client mandates the bank to invest their funds in assets, in their name and on their behalf, during a determined period, with or without restrictions.

"Moudharaba" is carried out according to the following two modalities:

*   "Restrictive Moudharaba," which consists, for the client, in mandating the bank to invest their funds in well-defined projects and according to agreed deadlines and conditions. In this case, the investment risk is borne by the client.
*   "Non-restrictive Moudharaba," which consists of giving the bank the freedom to invest the client's funds without any restriction.

**Article 13:** The return on investment deposits is linked to the results of the investment. **Article 15**: Every six months, the bank is required to inform its investment account holders of the nature of the investment operations carried out, their direct and indirect shares, as well as the profit and loss distribution arrangements.

**Title IV: General Provisions**

**Article 16**: The financing operations provided for in this circular may be subject to guarantees for the benefit of banks or financial institutions, in the form of mortgages, surety bonds, or other guarantees provided for by current legislation, to the extent that the use of these guarantees does not contradict the international standards of Islamic banking operations.

**Article 17**: The bank or financial institution may, before concluding any commercial financing contract, request from its client payment of an amount called a "seriousness deposit" equal to a determined percentage of the acquisition value. The "seriousness deposit" is intended to guarantee the execution of the contract and should be managed according to the conditions agreed upon between the bank or financial institution and the client.

**Article 18**: Banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of any financial product or service they intend to market within the framework of Islamic banking operations, in order to control their compliance with the international standards practiced in this field.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, within a period of ten working days from the communication of all the information it requests, oppose, by a reasoned decision, the marketing of the financial product or service.

**Article 19**: Banks and financial institutions are required, concerning Islamic banking contracts and operations, to comply with the international standards adopted in the field of Islamic banking operations. Article 20: The Central Bank of Tunisia oversees the compliance of Islamic banking operations with international standards practiced in this field.
To this end, banks and financial institutions engaging in Islamic banking operations must submit an annual report to the Central Bank of Tunisia on the control operations carried out by the Islamic banking standards compliance control committee, within a maximum period of one month before the holding of the general meeting of shareholders.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may request clarifications regarding the committee's opinion as well as the results of its work that are the subject of the aforementioned report. **CIRCULAR FROM THE CENTRAL BANK OF TUNISIA**

Article 2 - This circular is primarily part of the missions of supervising payment methods and taking measures likely to guarantee the stability, solidity, and efficiency of payment systems, which are devolved to the Central Bank of Tunisia by virtue of the aforementioned Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016. It applies to banks, payment institutions, and the National Postal Office, as well as to mobile Switch operators authorized by the Central Bank of Tunisia to carry out their activities.

When the persons referred to in the preceding paragraph subcontract certain operations related to mobile payment services or use the services of third parties, they must continuously ensure that the providers take all necessary measures to comply with the provisions of this circular.

Article 3 - For the purposes of this circular, the following are understood as:

- Institution: banks, payment institutions, and the National Postal Office.
- Wallet: a payment method made available to the customer by the institution, which allows for the storage of electronic money and the execution of payment operations via mobile phone, potentially including different technologies.
- Default Wallet: the wallet, among those available to a customer, on which funds received from a transfer or a payment to accepting merchants are automatically deposited.
- Mobile Payment: any payment transaction carried out from a mobile phone that results in a debit or credit movement on a Wallet, whether on a card, a bank account, a postal account, or a payment account. Mobile payment transactions include, in particular, operations following - Off-us transfer: Transactions carried out between users of mobile payment methods domiciled with two different institutions.
- Strong authentication: Two-factor authentication that combines the use of two elements from the following three categories: something you know (password, PIN), something you possess (computer, mobile phone), something you are (fingerprint, iris, voice...).
- User/client: "Mobile payment services user": a natural or legal person who uses a mobile payment service as a payer or a beneficiary, or both.
- Issuer: The institution that provides its client with payment methods to initiate mobile payment transactions.
- Acquirer: The institution that provides its client with services for acquiring mobile payment transactions.
- SGMT: Large amount transfer system managed by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

First Paragraph: General rules and conditions

Article 4 - The issuance and making available to the public by an institution of any payment method using a mobile phone must be:
- in compliance with the provisions of this circular and any other regulatory provision that concerns it; and
- carried out by affiliation to the mobile switch (Off Us) authorized to ensure the functionalities listed in the preceding article.
In the provision of mobile payment services, the institution remains subject to the requirements regarding the fight against the financing of terrorism and money laundering, and the protection of personal data.

Article 5 - Any institution must, one month before making available to the public any payment method using a mobile phone, submit to the Central Bank of Tunisia a file comprising, in particular: **Article 7 - In addition to legal requirements, the contract for the provision and use of a mobile payment instrument must stipulate, in particular, the following:**

*   The main services offered by mobile payment, including, free of charge for a fixed period and frequency, providing the customer with a clear statement of all mobile payment transactions, including the identification of the transaction, its value, the timestamp of its execution, as well as the amount of fees and commissions chargeable to them;
*   The customer's commitments, particularly regarding the designation of the default account for movements, identification, protection of access codes, compliance with security and confidentiality rules, and opposition procedures;
*   The issuer's commitments, particularly in terms of service continuity, security, complaint processing times, and the obligation to inform the customer of, among other things, service outages or unavailability;
*   The operational procedure of the service in clear and simple terms to enable financial education and to enhance the customer experience;
*   The pricing conditions in a transparent and clear manner;
*   The procedures for opposition, complaint processing, and chargeback;
*   The conditions and procedures for contract termination.

**Article 8 - The mobile switch manager must establish transparent and equitable conditions for establishments to join the mobile switch. They must define and make public the conditions for participation, suspension, and exclusion.**

The mobile switch manager must, to this end, conclude a standard agreement with the establishments which shall stipulate, in particular:

*   The services provided by the mobile switch;
*   The rights and obligations of the manager and the establishments, as well as, where applicable, of the users.

The participation agreement is subject to prior approval by - the claim must be registered in a dedicated database and listed with an identification reference;
- the customer must be given sufficient time, which must not be less than the legal time limit, to submit a claim, particularly to dispute an error in payment execution or an undue charge of a commission;
- the processing of claims cannot exceed a maximum period of 7 working days;
- in the event of a dispute, the mobile switch platform serves as the reference database for all "Off Us" transactions;
- the customer is promptly informed of any suspected fraudulent activity.
Article 13 - The establishment is required to refund the customer within legal deadlines, particularly in the following cases:
- operation carried out after the declaration of opposition;
- execution of operations not authorized by the customer or operations fraudulently executed by agents, employees, and service providers of the establishment;
- fraud due to a security issue.
Paragraph 2: Settlement, Clearing, and Pricing Rules
Article 14 - Payment services offered through the use of a mobile phone are instantaneous.
Transactions are irrevocable once validated by the originator.
The beneficiary and the originator are instantly notified of the transaction settlement by any means leaving a written trace.
Article 15 - The institution holding the account to which the payment method is linked must, immediately after the authorization of the transaction, credit the beneficiary's account, even before the actual receipt of funds from the clearing of external balances at the SGMT level.
The crediting of the customer's account must be carried out in compliance with:
- the caps for payment accounts, as defined by the provisions of circular n° 2018-16 of December 31, 2018, governing the activity and the f Article 19 - The following services must be provided free of charge:
- Subscription to the mobile payment service;
- Cash-in operations;
- Merchant payments for the paying customer;
- Balance and transaction details consultation;
- Termination of the mobile payment service.

Article 20 - Late mobile payment fees are not borne by the customer if the delay was caused by a planned service interruption of which the customer was not informed.

Article 21 - For any fund transfer and merchant payment operation referred to in Article 3 of this circular, inter-exchange fees cannot exceed 0.3% of the value of the operation.
Merchant payments, made with a mobile phone with a value less than or equal to 15 dinars, are exempt from any commission.
Switching services are charged by the mobile switch according to a fixed rate per operation.

Article 22 - Mobile payment service ecosystem actors must refrain from opposing interoperability.
They must refrain from participating in price-fixing agreements, sales quota or service provision agreements, calls for boycott, tied sales, and more generally any unfair and aggressive practice that has the consequence of hindering the free play of competition, particularly that which aims to oust a competitor from the market or restrict access to markets for new competitors.

Paragraph 3: Technical and Security Rules

Article 23 - The establishment must equip itself with an infrastructure compliant with the minimum requirements set by the Central Bank of Tunisia and with the standards that allow:
- connection to the mobile switch in compliance with the technical prerequisites and security requirements dictated by the Central Bank of Tunisia for this purpose;
- the sending and exchange of all payment flows via telephone **Article 25** - The mobile switch manager must ensure, among other things, the following functions:
- Management and updating of the customer reference mapping table;
- Routing of transactions based on the mapping table;
- Recording (tracing) of payment transaction settlement processes;
- Monitoring of balances and provision of data for clearing;
- Real-time notification to all institutions of any change to the default wallet;
- Transfer of balances resulting from the clearing of mobile payment transactions at the SGMT level;
- Monitoring of the mobile payment platform's operation and connections to other platforms.

**Article 26** - Mobile payment services are interoperable.
Issuing and acquiring institutions must implement the necessary technical prerequisites, particularly for interfacing with the mobile switch, to enable transaction interoperability.
Membership in the mobile switch is ensured according to the homologation process defined by the manager of this switch and approved by the Central Bank of Tunisia, before the operational deployment of the mobile payment service.

**Article 27** - "On Us" cinematics are freely managed by the institution, which has the freedom to choose its channels and technological tools.
In all cases, the institution must strive to ensure that user interfaces have a harmonized charter to offer a fluid and homogeneous user experience.

**Article 28** - The mobile switch manager ensures the proper functioning of the system and takes the necessary measures to guarantee availability and business continuity. Specifically, they must ensure:
- The permanent availability of switching services, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week;
- Instant confirmation to the payer upon payment validation;
- The routing Article 31 - The establishment and the manager of the mobile switch are required to take the necessary measures to ensure the security of the network and operational systems, and the establishment of a network and payment channels protected against fraud, piracy, and any other form of unauthorized use.
They must design and implement a cybersecurity program that addresses the various aspects of establishing an internal capability for the prevention, detection, and response to cyber incidents. The program must be aligned with international best practices and enable collaboration between them.

Article 32 - The establishment must identify and assess the security risks of mobile payment services and must continuously monitor these risks.
It must conduct periodic tests of security procedures and systems.

Article 33 - In order to protect the confidentiality and integrity of mobile payment user data, the establishment must:

- Secure interconnection with various partners through authentication, data encryption, traffic filtering and inspection, and intrusion detection.
- Define access rules and have access control systems that manage authorization identification, authentication, access approval, and entity accountability through login credentials.
- Restrict physical access to systems and limit access to customer data to authorized personnel.

Article 34 - The establishment is required to comply, at a minimum, with the following rules:

- Transactions can only be initiated after the prior steps of user authentication.
- Repeated entry of incorrect authentication information triggers a supplementary authentication mechanism or a block of the payment method. **Paragraph 4: Surveillance Reporting Rules**

**Article 39** - Institutions and the mobile switch are required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia without delay of any occurrence of cyber risks (fraud, intrusion, misuse of data, etc.) related to mobile payment methods, specifying:

*   The operational method of the incident and the identified points of fragility during the diagnostic performed for this purpose;
*   The number and, if applicable, the amount of fraudulent transactions carried out.

**Article 40** - Institutions and the mobile switch are required to report to the Central Bank of Tunisia, according to the terms and conditions it determines and no later than the end of the month following the close of each quarter, data in number and value relating to incidents of fraud, intrusion, and misuse that have occurred, whether committed within the institution or by external individuals.

**Article 41** - Institutions and the mobile switch must, each as far as they are concerned, report to the Central Bank of Tunisia, daily, according to the terms and conditions it determines, data relating to mobile payment activity, including commissions collected in number and value, broken down by instrument category and by nature of transaction.

**Article 42** - Institutions and the mobile switch are required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia without delay of any serious disruption to the continuity of mobile payment services that harms customers, specifying the nature of the incident and its extent in terms of duration and, if applicable, the damages caused. Decides:

Article 1: Subject
The purpose of this circular is to define the conditions for granting financial assistance by the Central Bank of Tunisia to banks and financial institutions, as provided for by Articles 19, 20, and 21 of Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, relating to the Statutes of the Central Bank of Tu **Article 6: Applicable Interest Rate**
The interest rate applicable to financial assistance operations shall be equal to the lending facility rate plus a margin of at least 250 basis points.

**Article 7: Duration of Financial Assistance**
Financial assistance is granted for a period not exceeding three months. However, the Central Bank of Tunisia may, if applicable, renew this assistance a maximum of three times, provided that the total duration of such assistance does not exceed 12 months and that the bank or financial institution meets, at the time of the renewal request, the eligibility conditions set out in Article 2 of this circular.

**Article 8: Eligible Assets and Guarantees**
The Central Bank of Tunisia may accept, within the framework of financial assistance, any asset or guarantee approved by its Board of Directors, by applying adequate haircuts set out in a bilateral agreement between the Central Bank of Tunisia and the bank or financial institution, as referred to in Article 9 of this circular.

**Article 9: Financial Assistance Agreement**
Before benefiting from financial assistance, the bank or financial institution must conclude an agreement with the Central Bank of Tunisia, which shall notably specify:

Article 1: A loan granted at an excessive interest rate is constituted by any conventional loan granted at an **overall effective interest rate** which exceeds, at the time it is granted, by more than one-fifth¹ the average effective rate practiced during the preceding semester by banks and financial institutions for operations of the same nature.

The Central Bank of Tunisia determines the operations that are subject to the same excessive interest rate.

Sales operations with payment facilities are assimilated to conventional loans and are subject to the provisions of this law.

Article 2: For the determination of the **overall effective interest rate** of the loan, account shall be taken, in addition to interest, of all fees, commissions, or remuneration of any kind, direct or indirect, incurred in the granting of the loan, except for those exempted by decree.

The methods for calculating the **overall effective interest rate** and the average effective rate, as well as their publication mode, are fixed by decree.

Article 3: The **overall effective interest rate** provided for by Article 2 of this law must be mentioned in any writing establishing a loan agreement governed by this law.

In the event that the said rate is not mentioned, the average effective interest rate practiced during the preceding semester will be taken into account, and the lender shall be liable to a fine ranging from five hundred to three thousand dinars.

Article 4: In case of the application of an excessive interest rate, the sums unduly received by the lender shall be returned to the borrower, increased by interest calculated at the legal rate provided for by Article 1100 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, from the date of their receipt.

The period rate is calculated actuarially, based on a unit period corresponding to the periodicity of payments made by the borrower. It ensures, according to the compound interest method, equality between, on the one hand, the sums lent and, on the other hand, all payments due by the borrower for this loan, in capital, interest, fees, commissions, or remuneration of any direct or indirect nature involved in granting credit, these elements being, where applicable, estimated.
The period rate is obtained by applying the following formula:

K: loan amount

P: reimbursement periodicity
t: period rate
n: number of reimbursement periods.

When the periodicity of payments is irregular, the unit period is that which corresponds to the shortest interval between two payments. The shortest calculation interval cannot, however, be less than one month.

Subject: Maintenance and administration of certificates of deposit accounts and treasury bill accounts.

TITLE ONE

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1: This circular sets out the conditions relating to the maintenance and administration of certificates of deposit accounts and treasury bill accounts issued on the money market.

Article 2: Certificates of deposit and treasury bills issued on the money market are dematerialized registered securities which must be entered in specific accounts opened in the name of each owner with:
- a credit institution, issuer or mandated, for certificates of deposit;
- a credit institution, mandated by the issuer, for treasury bills;
- a credit institution, administrator chosen by the owner.

Article 3: The maintenance and administration of certificates of deposit accounts and treasury bill accounts are exclusively carried out by credit institutions after signing the specifications forming the subject of Annexes No. 1 and No. 2 of this circular.
A duly signed copy of the specifications is deposited with the Central Bank of Tunisia (Directorate in charge of Capital Markets).

TITLE II

MAINTENANCE OF CERTIFICATES OF DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND TREASURY BILL ACCOUNTS

Article 4: The credit institution, issuer or mandated for the maintenance of securities accounts, must collect the following information from the account holder or the issuer of certificates of deposit or treasury bills:
- the name, first name, national identity card number, and address for individuals;
- the company name, legal form, registered office address, registration number. **Article 10:** The issuing or mandated credit institution must maintain a general ledger of transactions by security, based on double-entry bookkeeping, chronologically recording any entry affecting the accounts of registered holders with it. The ledger must precisely indicate, at all times, all transactions relating to the account. The ledger is referenced by the designation of the account(s) that were debited or credited.

The ledger must include, in particular:

*   The date of the transaction and the date of booking;
*   The nature of the transaction (debit or credit);

The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, establishing the status of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions,
