Having regard to Circular No. 91-24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 17, 1991, relating to the division, coverage of risks and monitoring of commitments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts,

Having regard to Circular No. 2018-10 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of November 1, 2018, on the "Loans/Deposits" ratio,

Having regard to the opinion of the Compliance Control Committee No. 2020-06 of March 19, 2020,

**Decides:**

**Article One** - Banks and financial institutions shall take all necessary measures within their purview to support businesses and professionals in facing the repercussions of the crisis linked to the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Article 2** - Banks and financial institutions shall postpone the payment of credit installments granted to businesses and professionals that are due, in principal and interest, during the period from March 1, 2020, to the end of September 2021, and revise the amortization schedule accordingly.

This measure applies to professional credits granted to clients classified as 0 and 1 as of December 31, 2019, within the meaning of Article 8 of Circular No. 91-24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 17, 1991, following a request submitted by any means leaving a written trace.

Banks and financial institutions may grant new financing. count in the calculation of the seniority of unpaid amounts within the meaning of Circular No. 91-24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia dated December 17, 1991, and this, for beneficiaries of support measures within the meaning of the present article.

Article 3 – Banks and financial institutions may extend the measures provided for in paragraph 1 of Article 2 of the present circular to clients classified as 2 and 3 as of the end of December 2019 within the meaning of Article 8 of Circular No. 91-24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia, and this, on a case-by-case basis following the assessment of the client's situation.

For beneficiaries of support measures within the meaning of the present article, the deferral period is not taken into account in the calculation of the seniority of unpaid amounts.

Article 4 – Repealed by Article 5 of Circular 2020-07 of March 25, 2020, relating to exceptional support measures for individuals.

Article 5 – Banks and financial institutions must communicate monthly to the Central Bank of Tunisia via the data exchange system, the list of beneficiaries of exceptional support measures (EXCEL file), in accordance with the table shown in Annex No. 1 of the present circular.

Article 6 – The present circular enters into force from the date of its publication. **Annex No. 1 to the Circular to Banks and Financial Institutions No. 2020 - 06 of March 19, 2020**

L **Article 1: General Provisions**
This circular sets out the conditions for implementing the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
Adherence to the conditions for implementing monetary policy as provided for in Annexes II, III, and IV of this circular is required for any counterparty to access monetary policy operations. Adherence is confirmed by the signature of the adherence form which is the subject of Annex I of this circular.
The practical arrangements and procedures for executing monetary policy operations are described in the Operations Manual, which is the subject of Annex II of this circular.
The provision of liquidity by the Central Bank of Tunisia is conditional upon the mobilization of appropriate collateral in its favor, in the form of negotiable assets and/or non-negotiable assets that meet the eligibility criteria as set by the Central Bank of Tunisia. The rules governing the mobilization of negotiable assets and non-negotiable assets are set out respectively in Annexes III and IV of this circular.

**Article 2: Eligible Counterparties**
The following conditions aim to allow a wide range of counterparties to access monetary policy operations according to uniform prudential and operational eligibility criteria.
Eligible counterparties for monetary policy operations are banks within the meaning of Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions, and which cumulatively meet the following conditions:
- They must be financially sound, in accordance with the assessment made by the Central Bank of Tunisia, particularly based on capital and liquidity ratios, regularly communicated by the banks; and
- They meet the operational criteria set by the Central Bank. Article 5: Categories of Operations Initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia

Operations initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia consist of four categories of operations defined as follows:

- **Main Refinancing Operations:** These operations constitute the main tool for providing liquidity by the Central Bank of Tunisia. They play a key role in steering interest rates and signal the orientation of monetary policy. The minimum interest rate applied to main refinancing operations is the key rate of the Central Bank of Tunisia. This is set by the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia in a manner consistent with the ultimate objective of price stability.

- **Longer-Term Refinancing Operations:** The purpose of these operations is to provide additional liquidity for maturities longer than that of main refinancing operations.

- **Fine-Tuning Operations:** These operations are carried out on a case-by-case basis to correct the effect of unforeseen fluctuations in banking liquidity on interest rates. They have a duration shorter than that of main refinancing operations.

- **Structural Operations:** These operations aim to manage a situation of durable liquidity deficit or surplus.

Article 6: Instruments for Executing Operations Initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia

Main refinancing operations and longer-term refinancing operations are exclusively carried out by means of repurchase agreements in the form of secured loans or reverse repurchase agreements as defined in Article 2 of the Monetary Policy Operations Manual, which is the subject of Annex II of this circular.

Article 15: Definition of Eligible Assets
In order to protect the balance sheet of the Central Bank of Tunisia against credit risk, refinancing operations are carried out on the basis of appropriate collateral.
To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia accepts negotiable assets, including public and private negotiable debt securities, and non-negotiable assets representing bank claims on companies and individuals, as collateral for refinancing operations, in accordance with the criteria established within the framework of this circular.

Article 16: Eligibility Criteria for Negotiable Assets
Negotiable assets accepted as collateral for refinancing operations must meet the following eligibility criteria:
- be negotiable debt instruments on the financial market and/or the money market. They must be admitted for operations by a central depository, namely Tunisie Clearing;
- be issued either by the Tunisian State or by a resident entity of public or private law with its headquarters in Tunisia;
- be denominated in Tunisian dinars;
- have a simple coupon structure, i.e., zero coupon, fixed coupon, or variable coupon indexed to a market rate. In all cases, the coupon structure must not lead to a negative cash flow;
- present a high credit quality in accordance with the selection criteria established by the Central Bank of Tunisia.
The Central Bank maintains a list of eligible negotiable assets, which can be consulted on the CAER system.

Article 17: Eligibility Criteria for Non-Negotiable Assets
Non-negotiable assets accepted as collateral for refinancing operations must meet the following eligibility criteria:
- be bank claims denominated in Tunisian dinars and representing a debtor's commitments to a counterparty Article 17 bis - Eligible Assets in Exceptional Circumstances
In exceptional circumstances, the Central Bank of Tunisia may accept, as collateral for refinancing operations, negotiable and non-negotiable assets that do not meet the eligibility criteria set out in Articles 16 and 17 of this circular and Articles 51 and 52 of its Appendix II.
The definition of exceptional circumstances and eligible assets will be published on the CAER system and the website of the Central Bank of Tunisia. (Added by banking circular no. 2020-10 of April 17, 2020)

Article 18: Mobilization of Eligible Assets
The mobilization of negotiable assets shall be carried out in accordance with the contractual provisions of the tripartite agreement signed between the Central Bank of Tunisia, the counterparty, and Tunisie Clearing (see Appendix III).
The mobilization of bank claims shall be carried out by their pledge as collateral, in accordance with the contractual provisions of the bilateral agreement signed between the Central Bank of Tunisia and the counterparty (see Appendix IV). Said pledge is made through the automated application of the Central Bank of Tunisia's Centralized Eligible Assets for Refinancing (CAER), in the form of electronic files.

Article 19: Valuation of Eligible Assets and Risk Control Measures
The Central Bank of Tunisia shall determine the value of assets serving as collateral for operations it carries out with eligible counterparties.
For any eligible asset traded on a market, the market price taken into account is that of the business day preceding the valuation date. In the absence of a representative market price, the Central Bank of Tunisia shall determine a theoretical price in accordance with commonly accepted financial asset valuation methods.

**Article 1**

**Subject and scope**

1. This Monetary Policy Operations Manual sets out the practical arrangements for the implementation of the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Tunisia (hereinafter referred to as the Central Bank), as defined by Chapter One of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank. The scope of this Manual does not include measures relating to the exercise of the Central Bank's powers outside of monetary policy: in particular, the scope of this Manual does not include measures relating to the oversight of payment systems and methods, such as intraday credit (Chapter 3 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank), financial stability, such as financial assistance (Chapter 4 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank), and foreign exchange policy and reserve management (Chapter 5 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank).

2. The Central Bank shall take all appropriate measures to implement its monetary policy operations in accordance with the principles, tools, instruments, conditions, criteria, and procedures set out in this Manual.

3. The Central Bank reserves the right to request from, and obtain from, counterparties any relevant information necessary for the accomplishment of its missions and the achievement of its objectives within the framework of monetary policy operations. This right is without prejudice to any other existing specific right of the Central Bank to request information relating to monetary policy operations.

Article 4
Overview of Categories and Instruments Concerning Operations Initiated by the Central Bank

1. The Central Bank may carry out operations on its own initiative for the purposes of steering interest rates, managing banking liquidity, and signaling the direction of monetary policy. The Central Bank decides on the terms of their execution and the instruments to be used.

2. Depending on their specific objective, operations initiated by the Central Bank may be grouped into the following categories:
a) Main refinancing operations;
b) Longer-term refinancing operations;
c) Fine-tuning operations;
d) Structural operations.

3. Operations initiated by the Central Bank are carried out using the following instruments:
a) Repurchase agreements;
b) "Reprise de liquidité en blanc" (reverse repurchase agreements or liquidity-absorbing operations);
c) Foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes;
d) Outright transactions;
e) Issuance of Central Bank of Tunisia debt certificates.

4. For the particular categories of operations initiated by the Central Bank defined in paragraph 2, the following instruments referred to in paragraph 3 may be used:
a) Main refinancing operations and longer-term refinancing operations are exclusively carried out by means of repurchase agreements in the form of secured loans or reverse repurchase agreements;
b) Fine-tuning operations may be carried out using the following instruments:
i. Repurchase agreements;
ii. Foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes;
iii. "Reprise de liquidité en blanc" (reverse repurchase agreements or liquidity-absorbing operations);
c) Structural operations may be carried out using the instruments 2. From the perspective of their operational characteristics, main refinancing operations:
a) Are liquidity-providing operations;
b) Are normally carried out weekly according to the indicative calendar for the regular tender operations of the Central Bank of Tunisia, subject to the exception provided for in paragraph 3;
c) Normally have a maturity of one week, as mentioned in the indicative calendar for the regular tender operations of the Central Bank of Tunisia, subject to the exception provided for in paragraph 3;
d) Are executed by means of tender procedures;
e) Are subject to counterparty eligibility criteria, which must be met by all counterparties submitting bids for these operations;
f) Are based on eligible assets used as collateral.

3. The maturity of main refinancing operations may vary depending on public holidays.

4. The Board of Directors of the Central Bank regularly decides on the interest rates applicable to main refinancing operations, and may furthermore amend them at any time. New interest rates apply at the earliest from the following business day.

5. Main refinancing operations are executed through fixed-rate tender procedures or multiple-rate tender procedures, in accordance with the decision of the Central Bank of Tunisia.

6. For main refinancing operations executed at a fixed rate, this latter normally corresponds to the central bank's key interest rate. For main refinancing operations executed at a multiple rate, the minimum bid rate is equal to the central bank's key interest rate.

The Marginal Lending Facility

Article 17

Characteristics of the Marginal Lending Facility

1. Counterparties may use the marginal lending facility to obtain twenty-four-hour liquidity from the Central Bank, through a repurchase agreement in the form of a secured loan or repo, at a predetermined interest rate by using eligible assets as collateral.

2. There is no limit to the amount of liquidity that can be provided under the marginal lending facility, as long as the obligation to provide appropriate collateral in accordance with paragraph 3 is met.

3. Assets presented by counterparties must be previously deposited with the Central Bank in the case of private claims or delivered at the time of application for access to the marginal lending facility in the case of negotiable securities. Failure to comply with this access condition shall result in penalties in accordance with Article 69 of this Manual.

Article 18

Conditions of Access to the Marginal Lending Facility

1. Counterparties meeting the eligibility criteria for counterparties and having an account with the Central Bank of Tunisia may access the marginal lending facility.

2. Access to the marginal lending facility is limited to days when the SGMT is operational. On days when securities settlement systems are not operational, access to the marginal lending facility is granted based on eligible assets that have already been previously deposited with the Central Bank.

3. To access the marginal lending facility, the counterparty must submit a request to the Central Bank. The Central Bank processes the request on the same day within the SGMT, provided that it receives the request no later than the provisional closing time of the SGMT. The deadline for submitting the request for access to the facil CHAPTER 2
The Deposit Facility

Article 20
Characteristics of the Deposit Facility

1. Counterparties may use the deposit facility to make overnight deposits with the Central Bank; a predetermined interest rate being applied to these deposits.

2. The Central Bank provides no collateral in exchange for the deposits.

3. There is no limit to the amount a counterparty can deposit under this facility.

Article 21
Conditions for Access to the Deposit Facility

1. Counterparties meeting the eligibility criteria for counterparties may access the deposit facility. Access to the deposit facility is limited to days when the TARGET system is operational.

2. To gain access to the deposit facility, the counterparty must submit a request to the Central Bank. The Central Bank processes the request on the same day within the TARGET system, provided it receives the request no later than the provisional closing time of TARGET. The deadline for submitting a request to access the deposit facility is extended by an additional fifteen minutes on the last business day of a reserve maintenance period. The request indicates the amount to be deposited under this facility.

Article 22
Duration and Interest Rate of the Deposit Facility

1. Deposits made under the deposit facility are for twenty-four hours. Deposits held under the deposit facility mature on the following day when the TARGET system is operational, at the opening of this system.

2. The interest rate applicable to the deposit is announced in advance by the Central Bank and is calculated in the form of a simple interest rate according to the "actual number of days/360" convention.

3. Interest on deposits is payable on the maturity of the deposit.

**Article 27**

Announcement of tender procedures

1. The Central Bank shall publicly announce tender procedures in advance through the Central Bank's data exchange system (SED) and/or financial information services. In addition, the Central Bank may announce tender procedures directly to counterparties if it deems it necessary.

2. The announcement of the tender shall constitute an invitation to counterparties to submit legally binding bids.

3. The information to be included in the public announcement of a tender procedure is set out in Annex II.1 of this Manual.

4. The Central Bank may take any action it deems appropriate to correct any potential 2. In fixed-rate tender procedures, counterparties indicate in their bids the amount they wish to obtain from the Central Bank.

3. In fixed-rate tender procedures concerning foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes, counterparties indicate the fixed amount of currency they wish to sell and repurchase, or buy and resell, at that rate.

4. In variable-rate tender procedures, counterparties are allowed to submit up to ten different bids in terms of interest rates, prices, or forward/swap rates. In exceptional cases, the Central Bank may impose an upper or lower limit on the number of bids each counterparty is allowed to submit. In each bid, counterparties indicate the amount they wish to trade and the corresponding interest rate, price, or forward/swap rate.

5. For variable-rate tender procedures concerning foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes, counterparties indicate the amounts in dinars and foreign currency, and the forward/swap rates at which they wish to conclude the operation.

6. For variable-rate tender procedures concerning foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes, the forward/swap rates are indicated in accordance with market conventions.

7. With regard to the issuance of Central Bank of Tunisia debt certificates, the latter may decide that bids be expressed in price rather than interest rate. In this case, prices are indicated as a percentage of the nominal price, with two decimal places.

1. The Central Bank rejects:

b) Any bid from a counterparty if the bid is below the minimum submission amount;

Sub-section 3
Allocation of the Auction

Article 33
Allocation in Fixed-Rate Tender Procedures for Providing or Withdrawing Liquidity

In a fixed-rate tender procedure, counterparty bids are allocated as follows:
a) Bids are added together;
b) If the total amount of bids exceeds the total amount of liquidity to be allocated, submissions are satisfied pro rata to the bids, based on the ratio between the amount to be allocated and the total amount of bids;
c) The amount allocated to each counterparty is rounded to the nearest million dinars.

Article 34
Allocation in Multiple-Rate Tender Procedures for Providing Liquidity

In a multiple-rate tender procedure for providing liquidity, counterparty bids are allocated as follows:
a) The list of submissions is established in descending order of offered interest rates or ascending order of offered prices;
b) Bids with the interest ra **Article 35**

**Adjudication during multi-rate tender procedures intended to withdraw liquidity**

In a multi-rate dinar tender procedure intended to withdraw liquidity, used for the issuance of debt certificates and the repurchase of unencumbered liquidity, counterparties' bids are awarded as follows:

a) The list of submissions is established in ascending order of offered interest rates or in descending order of offered prices;
b) Bids with the lowest interest rate (highest price) are satisfied first, then bids with higher interest rates (lower price bids) are subsequently accepted until the total amount of liquidity to be withdrawn is exhausted;
c) If, at the marginal interest rate (lowest accepted price), the global amount of bids exceeds the residual amount to be awarded, the latter is awarded pro rata to these bids based on the ratio between the residual amount to be awarded and the total amount of bids at the marginal interest rate (lowest accepted price);
d) The amount allocated to each counterparty is rounded to the nearest million dinars. Regarding the issuance of debt certificates by the Central Bank of Tunisia, the nominal amount allocated is rounded to the nearest thousand dinar multiple.

**Article 36**

**Adjudication during multi-rate tender procedures concerning foreign exchange swaps intended to provide liquidity**

In a multi-rate foreign exchange swap tender procedure intended to provide liquidity, counterparties' bids are awarded as follows:

a) The list of submissions is established in descending order of forward/backwardation rates, taking into account the sign of the quotation;
b) The sign of the quotation depends on the sign of the interest rate differential between the foreign currency and the dinar. For the swap maturity b) The sign of the quotation depends on the sign of the interest rate differential between the currency and the dinar. For the swap maturity:

i. If the currency's interest rate is higher than the corresponding interest rate for the dinar, the forward/backwardation rate is negative, meaning the dinar is quoted in forward against the currency; and
ii. If the currency's interest rate is lower than the corresponding interest rate for the dinar, the forward/backwardation rate is positive, meaning the dinar is quoted in backwardation against the currency;

c) Bids with the lowest forward/backwardation rates are satisfied first; subsequent, higher bids are then accepted until the total amount of dinars to be repurchased is exhausted.

d) If, at the highest accepted forward/backwardation rate (i.e., the marginal forward/backwardation rate), the aggregate amount of bids exceeds the residual amount to be awarded, the latter is awarded pro rata to the bids, based on the ratio between the residual amount to be awarded and the total amount of bids at the marginal forward/backwardation rate.

e) The amount awarded to each counterparty is rounded to the nearest million dinars.

Article 38

Type of Auction for Multiple-Rate Tender Procedures

For multiple-rate tender procedures, the Central Bank normally uses a "Dutch" auction (multiple-rate auction).

**Article 50**

**Assets Eligible for Guarantee Purposes**

1. Credit operations carried out by the Central Bank require the pledging of eligible assets by counterparties to guarantee the amounts of credit granted. Credit operations include repurchase agreements and intraday overdrafts granted within the framework of the payment system (SGMT).

2. The conditions for accessing intraday overdrafts are set by the intraday repurchase agreement (PLI) convention signed between the Central Bank and the counterparties within the framework of the general accession agreement to the SGMT.

3. The Central Bank accepts two categories of eligible assets to guarantee liquidity provision operations in the form of repurchase agreements:

    a) negotiable assets including public and private negotiable debt securities; and
    b) non-negotiable assets representing bank claims on companies and individuals resident in Tunisia.

4. Counterparties provide eligible assets:

    a) through the transfer of ownership of negotiable debt securities, by entry in the BCT's securities account, which legally takes the form of a secured loan or a repurchase agreement; and

    b) through the establishment of a pledge or assignment on bank claims, which legally takes the form of a secured loan.

**MEASURES TAKEN IN CASE OF BREACH OF COUNTERPARTIES' OBLIGATIONS**

**Article 67**

**Penalties for breaches concerning mandatory reserves**

Any shortfall compared to the amount required for the mandatory reserve shall result in the collection by the Central Bank of interest calculated over the reserve formation period at the rate of the standing lending facility plus 2.5 percentage points.

**Article 68**

**Measures taken in case of breaches of certain operational rules**

1. In accordance with the contractual provisions applied by the Central Bank, measures shall be taken against counterparties who breach any of the following obligations:

    a) With regard to repurchase agreements and foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes, the obligations to adequately guarantee and settle the amount awarded to the counterparty throughout the duration of a specific operation, in accordance with Article 14;
    b) With regard to fine-tuned liquidity-absorbing operations, firm transactions and the issuance of debt certificates by the Central Bank of Tunisia, the obligation to settle the transaction, in accordance with Article 15;
    c) With regard to the use of eligible assets, the obligation to only pledge or use eligible assets and to comply with the rules for the use of eligible assets set out in Part Three;
    d) With regard to end-of-day procedures and conditions for accessing the marginal lending facility, the obligation to provide sufficient eligible assets as collateral in cases where a debit balance remains on a counterparty's settlement account in the SGMT after the completion of end-of-day control procedures;
    e) With regard to the Central Bank's right to request and obtain from counterparties any relevant information. The Central Bank suspends the counterparty's access upon the third breach and upon each subsequent breach of an obligation of the same type during the twelve-month period concerned. The twelve-month period is calculated from the date of the first breach of an obligation referred to in Article 68, paragraph 1, point a) or b), as applicable.

2. Any suspension imposed by the Central Bank under paragraph 1 applies to any monetary policy operation initiated by the Central Bank thereafter.

3. The suspension period imposed under paragraph 1 is determined in accordance with Annex II.4.

4. If a counterparty fails to comply with an obligation referred to in Article 68, paragraph 1, point c), on more than two occasions during a twelve-month period, and for each breach:
a) A penalty was applicable;
b) Each decision to impose a penalty was notified to the counterparty;
c) Each case of breach concerns the same type of breach;

The Central Bank suspends the counterparty's access to the next operation initiated by the Central Bank upon the third breach and upon each subsequent breach during the twelve-month period concerned. The twelve-month period is calculated from the date of the first breach of an obligation referred to in Article 68, paragraph 1, point c).

5. In exceptional cases, the Central Bank may suspend a counterparty's access, for a period of three months, to all future monetary policy operations of the Central Bank in the event of a breach of any of the obligations provided for in Article 68, paragraph 1. In such a case, the Central Bank shall take into account the seriousness of the case and, in particular, the amounts involved as well as the frequency and duration of the breach.

6. The suspension period imposed by the Central Bank under this article applies in **PART FIVE**

**Article 71**

Discretionary measures taken under the precautionary principle or following a case of default

1. Under the precautionary principle, the Central Bank may take any of the following discretionary measures:

a) Suspend, limit, or prohibit a counterparty's access to operations initiated by the Central Bank or to standing facilities;

b) Refuse assets pledged as collateral for central bank credit operations by a given counterparty, limit their use, or apply additional haircuts to them, based on any information deemed relevant by the Central Bank, particularly if the counterparty's credit quality is closely correlated with the credit quality of the pledged assets.

2. Where a measure initiated by the Central Bank, as described in paragraph 1, is based on prudential information, the Central Bank shall use such information to the extent strictly necessary for the performance of its monetary policy tasks.

3. In the event of a default, the Central Bank may suspend, limit, or prohibit access to operations initiated by the Central Bank or to the Central Bank's standing facilities for counterparties in default.

4. All discretionary measures taken under paragraphs 1 and 3 shall be applied in a proportionate and non-discriminatory manner and shall be duly justified by the Central Bank. SIXTH PART, FINAL PROVISIONS

Regulation in matters of fighting against money laundering and terrorism financing

LIST OF OPERATIONS ELIGIBLE FOR FINANCING BY MEDIUM-TERM AGRICULTURAL CREDITS (1)

a) Acquisition of new agricultural equipment:

- Tractors for agricultural work
- Harvesting equipment, notably combine harvesters and binder harvesters
- Spreading, sowing, fertilizing, and crop protection equipment.
- Soil tillage implements, notably plows, disc harrows, etc.
- Specialized equipment for harvesting, collecting, and conditioning fodder and forage seeds.
- Transport equipment, animal or mechanical traction (trailers, mobile tankers, etc.).
- Soil tillage implements
- Greenhouses

b) Acquisition of breeding stock:

- Purchase of cattle: purebred heifers, imported in calf or born and raised in Tunisia, crossbred heifers in calf, local heifers in calf from artificial insemination or from an approved bull, bulls.
- Purchase of sheep.
- Purchase of bee colonies.

c) Acquisition of specialized livestock equipment:

- Dairy equipment
- Sheepfold equipment
- Hives and beekeeping equipment.

d) Construction of livestock buildings.

The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Considering Law n°2016 -35 of April 25, 2016 establishing the status of the Central Bank of Tunisia;
Considering Law n°2016 -48 of July 11, 2016 relating to banks and financial institutions;
Considering Circular n°87 -47 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 23, 1987 on the modalities for granting, controlling, and refinancing of credits, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts;
Considering Circular n°91 -24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 17, 1991 relating to the division, coverage of risks, and monitoring of commitments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts;
Considering Circular n°2017 -02 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of March 10, 2017 relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia,
Considering the opinion of the Compliance Control Committee n° 12 -2019 of December 18, 2019,

Decides:

Article One - Banks and financial institutions may proceed with the rescheduling of principal and interest payment deadlines for credits granted to oil producers and olive oil exporters who have encountered difficulties in repaying their debts during the 2017/2018 and 2018/2019 campaigns.
The rescheduling shall be done on a case-by-case basis and for a duration that takes into account the repayment capacity of each beneficiary.
Banks and financial institutions may grant new financing to beneficiaries of rescheduled credits for the 2019/2020 campaign.

Article 2 - Banks and financial institutions that have proceeded with rescheduling and granting new financing within the meaning of Article One of this circular may, during the year 2019, maintain the classification determined at f Article 3 - Banks and financial institutions must, when calculating collective provisions, assign the oil producers sector and the olive oil export sector to specific categories within the reference methodology for calculating these provisions, as provided for in Annex 3 of the Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia No. 91-24 of December 17, 1991, while applying the following minimum provisioning rates:

| Sectors                   | Minimum Provision Rate |
| :------------------------ | :--------------------- |
| Oil Producers             | 35%                    |
| Olive Oil Exporters       | 30%                    |

Article 4 - Banks and financial institutions are required to communicate monthly to the Central Bank of Tunisia, via the data exchange system, the list of companies that have benefited from treatment measures, indicating the nature of the measure, in accordance with the table that forms the annex to this circular.

Article 5 - This circular comes into force as of the date of its publication. **Annex to Circular to Banks and Credit Institutions No. 2019-12 of December 18, 2019**

**SUBJECT: Improvement of the coverage rate of agricultural activities financed by bank loans with an insurance system.**

**Article 1**: The financing of agricultural projects and activities requires the beneficiary to obtain insurance coverage within the limits of the risks covered by insurance companies.

**Article 2**: The cost of insurance is included in the components of agricultural projects financed by medium and long-term loans and will be calculated in the total cost of the investment.

**Article 3**: For short-term seasonal crop loans, the cost of insurance is reimbursed from the first installment of the loan.

**Article 4**: Banks shall conclude contracts with insurance companies that determine the conditions and methods for collecting insurance premiums, as well as the compensation amounts.

**Article 5**: This circular takes effect from its date. **NOTE TO BANKS N° 96-25**

**Article 1: For the purposes of the refinancing regulations, investments in resident exporting industries and in small and medium-sized enterprises are respectively considered as:**

Article 3: Operations are carried out on the money market in accordance with the following procedures:
- The first dash of Article 3 is repealed by circular n°2018-12 of November 28, 2018
- Loans from credit institutions to moral persons under public or private law or to natural persons are made by means of registered debt securities negotiable by account transfer, known as certificates of deposit;
- Liquidity exchanges between companies or with natural persons, which can only take place through banks, are made by means of registered debt securities negotiable by account transfer, known as treasury bills.

Article 4: Certificates of deposit may only be issued by credit institutions and must:
- be registered in the name of the subscriber and issued at par;
- be registered in an account with a credit institution in the name of the subscriber;
- have a minimum nominal amount representing a multiple of five hundred (500) thousand dinars;
- have a fixed maturity date;
- have a duration of at least ten (10) days and at most five (5) years. This duration must be a multiple of ten (10) days, months, or years;
- be subject to remuneration at a fixed rate, freely determined at the time of issue for durations less than or equal to one year, and at a fixed or variable rate for durations greater than one year. The method of payment of this remuneration and the formula to be applied for its calculation are set out in Article 7 of this circular. - companies benefiting from a backup line that allows the issuer to meet cash needs that could not be covered due to the impossibility of renewing previous issues, stemming from the money market situation and no other reason. The granting of this line by the bank does not constitute a guarantee;
- companies belonging to a group of companies when the subscribers are part of that same group; and
- companies governed by specific legal provisions.

**Article 6: Treasury bills must:**

- be registered and issued at par;
- be held in an account with a credit institution in the name of the subscriber;
- have a minimum nominal amount representing a multiple of fifty (50) thousand dinars;
- have a fixed maturity date;
- have a term of at least ten (10) days and a maximum of five (5) years. This term must be a multiple of ten (10) days, months, or years;
- be subject to remuneration at a fixed rate, freely determined at the time of issuance for terms less than or equal to one year, and at a fixed or variable rate for terms greater than one year. The method of payment of this remuneration and the formula to be applied for its calculation are fixed by Article 7 of this circular;
- be domiciled with a bank.

Treasury bills cannot include a redemption premium.

**Article 7: For certificates of deposit or treasury bills with a term of one year or less, the interest is payable in advance and calculated according to the following formula:**

```
        ctn
I = -----------
       (36000 + tn)
```

**With:**

I: amount of interest;
c: amount of the security;
t: interest rate;
n: exact number of days from the day of subscription Article 8 bis2 - Certificates of deposit and treasury bills must be codified and admitted to the operations of the central securities depository referred to by the order of the Minister of Finance of January 12, 2016, approved by the regulation of the Financial Market Council relating to the central securities depository, and this according to the conditions and procedures applicable to it.

**Article 1**: Treasury bills are debt instruments issued by the State within the framework of the budgetary balance provided for by the finance law.

**Article 2**: Treasury bills are issued through auctions announced to banks operating on the money market through the Central Bank of Tunisia. The auction will determine, among other things, the indicative amount of each issuance and the characteristics of the bills to be subscribed.

**Article 3**: Submissions to auctions are made by the aforementioned banks. These banks may subscribe to treasury bills both for their own account and for the account of a third natural or legal person.

Subscriptions are settled in a single payment to the benefit of the public Treasury.

**Article 51**: The interest paid on treasury bills is determined on the basis of fixed rates established according to the offers presented by the banks during each auction.

After processing the submissions, treasury bills are allocated to banks starting with the offers at the lowest interest rates.

However, a limited proportion of each submission, fixed at the announcement of each auction, may be reserved for non-competitive bids presented by banks on behalf of their clients.

These non-competitive bids will be served at the weighted average rate of the accepted submissions.

The interest on treasury bills is discounted on the basis of a 360-day year and is paid in arrears.

TITLE ONE

Article 1: Treasury bonds, which are securities issued by the State representing loans within the framework of budgetary balance, are negotiable with all banks operating in the money market. The unit value of each bond is set at one thousand dinars.

Article 2: Treasury bonds are managed in current accounts opened in the books of the Central Bank of Tunisia in the name of the subscribing banking establishments.

Article 3: The maturity date of Treasury bonds is communicated to banks on the occasion of each auction. The duration of the bonds can notably be 13, 26, 52 weeks and more than one year.

Article 4: The interest rate applied to Treasury bonds is fixed and results from the banks' bids. For bonds with a duration of one year or less, interest is settled upon subscription and calculated according to the following formula:
I = [CTN / (36000 + TN)]

where:
I: amount of interest;
C: nominal value of the Treasury bond;
T: interest rate;
N: exact number of days from the issue date to the maturity date, with one of these two dates included in the calculation.

For bonds with a duration of more than one year, interest is settled annually at term, based on a 360-day year, using the following formula:
I = [CTN / 36000]

where:
I: amount of interest;
C: nominal value of the Treasury bond;
T: interest rate;
N: exact number of days from the issue date to the maturity date, with one of these two dates included in the calculation.

**Margin Management**

**1. Determination of the value difference of a delivery pension convention with margin and the net balance of each party:**

**1.1.** On each valuation date, the calculation agent shall determine, for each delivery pension convention with margin outstanding on that date, the positive or negative difference between:

(i) the value of the securities delivered under a repurchase agreement, adjusted by the initial safety margin (if any); and

(ii) the sale price of the said securities increased by the accrued interest thereon, calculated at the rate of the delivery pension convention, from the date of sale (inclusive) to the valuation date under consideration (exclusive).

**1.2.** Once this difference has been determined, the calculation agent shall calculate for each party the value difference of each outstanding delivery pension convention with margin, which shall be equal to:

(i) for any delivery pension convention for which the party concerned is the seller, to the difference between the two amounts referred to above, and of the same sign as this difference;

(ii) for any delivery pension convention for which the party concerned is the buyer, to the difference between the two amounts referred to above, but with the opposite sign.

**1.3.** Once the value difference of each delivery pension convention with margin has been determined, the calculation agent shall determine the net balance of the value differences of each party (hereinafter referred to as the "net balance"), which shall be equal to the algebraic sum of the value differences of that party for each of the outstanding delivery pension conventions with margin.

**2. Provision or retrocession of margin based on the net balance:**

**2.1.** On each valuation date, the calculation agent shall request the party with a negative net balance to provide a margin in favor of the party with a positive net balance, with a value equal to that net balance. **ANNEX N°2 TO CIRCULAR N°2013 -05 OF APRIL 30, 2013**

**Subject: Interbank Market in Dinars**

Having regard to Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, fixing the statute of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions,

Having regard to Law No. 2012-24 of December 24, 2012, relating to the repurchase agreement,

Having regard to Circular to Credit Institutions No. 2005-09 of July 14, 2005, relating to the organization of the money market, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts,

Having regard to Circular to Credit Institutions and Authorized Intermediaries No. 2008-07 of March 13, 2008, relating to the use of the "SED" data exchange system,

Having regard to the Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia No. 2013-05 of April 30, 2013, concerning a framework agreement for repurchase agreements,

Having regard to Circular to Banks No. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to the deliberation of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia dated June 13, 2018,

Having regard to Opinion No. 10-2018 of the Control and Compliance Committee dated November 16, 2018, as provided for by Article 42 of Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, fixing the statute of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

**Decides:**

**TITLE ONE: SUBJECT, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS**

**Article 1: Subject and Scope**
The purpose of this circular is to define the conditions, procedures, and processes for liquidity exchange within the interbank market in dinars. It applies to banks as defined by Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions.

**Article 2: Definitions**
"Contributing Bank": a bank that is part of the panel of contributors to TUNIBOR.
"Underlying Contributions to TUNIBOR": "SGMT," the Tunisian large-value payment system, enabling gross real-time settlement of payments in dinar.

"Trading System," a secure and reliable system for the electronic trading of interbank transactions.

"Reference Interest Rates," interest rates calculated and published daily by the Central Bank of Tunisia, applying a formula to underlying data from interbank transactions or contributions made by the panel of TUNIBOR contributors.

"TM," the average overnight interest rate on the interbank market.

"Unsecured Interbank Transaction," an interbank transaction without collateral.

"Interbank Transaction," an exchange of liquidity concluded between two banks in the form of an unsecured transaction or a repurchase agreement.

"TUNIBOR," abbreviation for 'Tunisian interbank offered rate,' representing the average interest rate at which contributing banks are willing to grant each other unsecured loans for each of the maturities ranging from one week to twelve months: one week, two weeks, one month, two months, three months, six months, nine months, and twelve months.

TITLE II: QUOTING, TRADING, AND REPORTING OF INTERBANK TRANSACTIONS

Article 3: Obligation to Display Quotations

Banks are required to continuously display their indicative bid and ask conditions for liquidity in dinar for maturities ranging from overnight to one year. This obligation also applies to banks engaged in operations consistent with the principles of Islamic finance as provided for by current regulations, particularly Articles 11 to 16 of Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions.

The display of rate quotations must be carried out through contribution pages broadcast over secure information networks. **Article 7: Negotiation of Interbank Transactions**
Regardless of the form that the exchange of liquidity in dinars takes on the interbank market, banks are
required to use a trading system that guarantees the traceability and security of transactions, such as
Reuters or Bloomberg.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may remotely access real-time data on interbank transactions
carried out via the said trading system without prior authorization from the
banks.

**Article 8: Declarations of Interbank Transactions by Banks**
Banks are required to declare to the Central Bank of Tunisia, for each category indicated in
Article 6 of this circular, interbank transactions carried out per session, in accordance with
the IT recording structure published on the Data Exchange System (SED).
During the double-session period, two declaration sessions are set for no later than 10:30 AM and 2:00 PM.
For the single-session period, one declaration session is set for no later than 10:30 AM. In case of malfunction
of the Data Exchange System (SED), banks may use fax or, if applicable, any other
communication system that leaves a written record.
Banks must also communicate to the Central Bank of Tunisia, no later than 15 minutes after
the provisional closing of the Tunisia Large Value Payment System (SGMT), a summary of all
interbank transactions for the day, specifying, for each category, the amounts, rates, and durations
processed.

**Article 9: Information Communicated by the Central Bank of Tunisia**
At the end of each session provided for in Article 8 of this circular, the Central Bank of Tunisia
communicates to the banks a file, for each category of operations, summarizing all
transactions declared, broken down by amount, rate, and duration. **Article 11: Calculation Methodology for the Overnight Average Interest Rate (TM)**

The overnight average interest rate (TM) is calculated as a weighted average of the overnight lending rates of all interbank unsecured transactions, transmitted at the end of the day to the Central Bank of Tunisia under the conditions set out in Article 8 of this circular. This rate is rounded to the nearest basis point. The Central Bank of Tunisia reserves the right to eliminate outlier rates that do not reflect market conditions.

**Article 12: Publication of the TM**

The overnight average interest rate (TM) is published at the end of each day by the Central Bank of Tunisia on the data exchange system (SED), and no later than the following day on its website and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

**Article 13: Panel of TUNIBOR Contributors**

The panel of TUNIBOR contributors comprises the most active banks in the dinar money market that meet the eligibility criteria for counterparties in monetary policy operations as provided for in Article 2 of Circular No. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, concerning the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia.
To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia ranks banks at least once a year based on the volume of activity carried out in the various segments of the dinar money market (interbank market, negotiable debt securities market, and refinancing with the Central Bank of Tunisia).
The Central Bank of Tunisia regularly publishes and updates the list of TUNIBOR contributing banks on its website and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

**Article 14: Obligations Incumbent on Contributing Banks**

Each contributing bank is required to update its quotations daily before 10:45 AM. The Central Bank of Tunisia ensures that at least half of the banks in the panel of contributors have communicated their lending rates for the 8 maturities before 10:45 AM. If this quorum is not met, the Central Bank of Tunisia may postpone the fixing time for TUNIBOR and informs the market accordingly.

The methodology for calculating TUNIBOR may be modified by the Central Bank of Tunisia, after consulting the banks, to better reflect market realities.

**Article 16: Publication of TUNIBOR**

TUNIBOR is published every working day at 11:00 AM on the website of the Central Bank of Tunisia and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

**TITLE IV: FINAL PROVISIONS**

**Article 17: Measures taken in case of default**

The obligations provided for in this circular, incumbent upon the banks, constitute conditions for the implementation of monetary policy within the meaning of circular no. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia. Failure to comply with any of these obligations is subject to the measures provided for in the said circular against the counterparties.

**Article 18: Repeal**

Title One, as well as the provisions of the first dash of Article 3, Article 18, and the first paragraph of Article 20 of circular no. 2005-09 of July 14, 2005, relating to the organization of the money market, are hereby repealed.

**Article 19: Entry into force**

This circular enters into force on January 02, 2019. ANNEX N°1 TO CIRCULAR N°2018 -12 OF NOVEMBER 28, 2018

CHAPTER 4

Article 10: Credit institutions must constitute provisions at least equal to 20% for class 2 assets, 50% for class 3 assets, and 100% for class 4 assets.

These provisions must be specifically allocated to any classified asset equal to or greater than 50,000 dinars.⁴ It is understood that the constitution of provisions takes into account guarantees received from the State, insurance organizations, and credit institutions, as well as guarantees in the form of deposits or financial assets that can be liquidated without affecting their value. Movable and immovable property given as collateral by borrowers are considered valid guarantees only if the credit institution has a duly registered mortgage and independent and frequent valuations of these collateral are available. Furthermore, the possibility of rapid liquidation on the market at the valuation price must be ensured.

**PROVISIONS RELATING TO OVERDRAFT**

**Article 11:** Excluding structural deficits, cash flow needs, even if repetitive, arising from discrepancies between revenue and expenditure flows, may be subject to an overdraft for an amount between fifteen and thirty days of turnover.
Beyond this amount, banks must put in place credit facilities whose form and duration are better suited to the real needs of the company.
Amounts not justified by these needs must be reclaimed from the beneficiaries for immediate settlement.
In cases where immediate settlement proves difficult to achieve, the said amounts will be subject, only once, to a repayment schedule for principal and interest.
The characteristics of classes 2, 3, and 4, as defined in Article 8 of this circular, are applicable to overdrafts.
When a period of 90 days has elapsed after the interest has been calculated without the account recording revenue movements likely to offset the full amount of debit interest and other charges, the overdraft (or debit account) is generally considered frozen and must be included in class 2.
When this period exceeds 180 days but does not exceed 360 days, the overdraft must be included in class 3. Beyond a period of 360 days, the overdraft must be included in class 4.

For classified overdrafts, banks must only incorporate into their results the interest actually received. Any previously recorded but unpaid interest is deducted from the results.

Methodology for determining collective provisions
(REPEALED AND REPLACED BY CIRCULAR TO BANKS AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS N°2024 -01 OF JANUARY 19, 2024)

This methodology is based on the following steps:
I. Determination of the calculation base for collective provisions
Gross on-balance sheet commitments and off-balance sheet commitments, excluding notified and unused credits, classified as 0 and 1 at the end of the reference year designated "Nr".
Commitments to banks, financial institutions within the meaning of Law n°2016 -48, as well as microfinance institutions constituted in the form of a public limited company, are excluded.

II. Grouping of commitments 0 and 1 into homogeneous groups
Commitments of the target population are grouped by customer segment and by sector of activity.
* Commitments from private sector professionals
- Agriculture
- Mechanical and electrical industries
- Agri-food industries, including oil crushers
- Pharmaceutical industries
- Other industries
- Construction and Public Works (BTP)
- Tourism, including travel agencies
- Real estate development
- Commerce
- Health
- Telecom and ICT
- Other services, including car rental agencies

* Public counterparties
- Public companies operating in competitive sectors
- Other public bodies

* Individuals
- Private sector individuals: Housing loans
- Private sector individuals: Consumer loans

**SUBJECT: Terms of Reference for the Audit of Accounts.**

The Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia n°91-24 dated December 17, 1991, defined, in its Article 14, the objectives of the supervisory mission of statutory auditors (or auditors) of banks.

To this end, statutory auditors (or auditors) must expressly provide, within their reports, their conclusions on:

*   The internal control systems implemented by the bank,
*   The accounting principles applied to various operations and the justification of accounts,
*   Credit policies, debt recovery, and the monitoring of commitments,
*   The valuation of assets included on or off the balance sheet,
*   The accounting for income from credit operations and provisions made for the coverage of risks.

In addition, statutory auditors (or auditors) must issue independent opinions and detailed reports relating to the following annual financial statements:

*   Balance sheet as of the end of the year,
*   Income statement for the financial year ending at the end of the same year,
*   Profit and loss account for the same financial year,
*   Cash flow statement for the same financial year.

These reports and opinions must be prepared in accordance with the standards of the Order of Chartered Accountants of Tunisia, as well as the recommendations of the International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC) and those of the IFAC.

The reports to be provided by statutory auditors (or auditors) to the Central Bank of Tunisia must contain the following documents, including a sufficient number of details and annexes to support the conclusions and opinions reached by the auditors:

1°) Financial statements 9°) An assessment of foreign exchange risk. The statutory auditors (or auditors) must determine the extent of actual and potential foreign exchange risk losses and evaluate the adequacy of information systems in identifying foreign exchange risks and the accounting procedures used to reflect them.

10°) An assessment of interest rate risk and liquidity management (assets and liabilities); the statutory auditors (or auditors) must report on any significant risk related to changes in interest or liquidity rates to assess management's ability to manage loss risks.

11°) an opinion on the adequacy of capital. To the extent that capital is inadequate to support current and future operations, the auditor shall recommend the amount of additional capital required.

SCOPE AND TERMS OF THE AUDIT

The work of the statutory auditors (or auditors) must be carried out in accordance with generally accepted accounting practices for fieldwork and data communication. In this regard, the statutory auditors (or auditors) must:

1°) Plan and execute their work based on an audit program sufficiently extensive to cover the activities of the bank or financial institution in their charge.

2°) Comment on the accounting principles adopted by the bank or financial institution, particularly to confirm or deny if, and to what extent, generally accepted accounting principles and standards are applied regularly, and to specifically indicate the adoption of any other principle and its impact on the annual financial statements.

3°) Take into account, when preparing the report(s), the implementation and reliability of administrative procedures and c 8°) Ensure the sincerity and regularity of the financial statements provided. When the financial statements do not reflect the true and fair view of the bank's or financial institution's situation, the statutory auditors (or auditors) must detail and quantify the necessary adjustments. Emphasis should be placed on: (a) the adequacy of loss provisions and the necessary adjustments to bring valuation provisions to adequate levels; (b) adjustments to profit and loss accounts relating to recognized income from assets in classes 2, 3, and 4; (c) adjustments to profit and loss accounts for accrued and unpaid interest that has been capitalized, renegotiated, or refinanced; and (d) extraordinary or non-recurring income.

9°) Identify, quantify, and assess credit concentrations, with an emphasis on credit granted to: (a) insiders of the institution and their related interests (shareholders, directors, and executives); (b) parties related to the bank, including subsidiaries and affiliates; and (c) major economic sectors. They only allow for the recovery of provisions already constituted in the case of guarantee consolidation and compliance with the new reimbursement schedule.

Interest that is reserved or deferred, having been the subject of an arrangement, rescheduling, or consolidation, must not be incorporated into the results of the financial year to which the arrangement, rescheduling, or consolidation relates. Only the portion actually collected is incorporated into the results of the financial year.

In the case of new payment incidents, unpaid amounts must be fully provisioned. If the cumulative unpaid principal reaches 25% of the total claim, the claim must be classified in class 4.

**CONSTITUTION OF PROVISIONS**

Banks must constitute provisions of at least 20% for class 2 assets, 50% for class 3 assets, and 100% for class 4 assets.

These provisions must be specifically allocated to any asset classified at 50 thousand dinars or more, or 0.5% of net equity.

It is understood that the constitution of provisions takes into account guarantees received from the State, insurance organizations, and banks, as well as guarantees in the form of deposits or financial assets that can be liquidated without affecting their value.

Movable and immovable property given as security by borrowers are only considered valid guarantees if the bank has a duly registered mortgage and independent and frequent valuations of these guarantees are available. Furthermore, **INDIVIDUAL SHEET**

SUBJECT: Rules relating to the monitoring of foreign exchange positions.

TITLE ONE
DEFINITION AND DETERMINATION OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE POSITION

Article 1: The foreign exchange position in a given currency is defined as the balance of assets in that currency resulting from spot and forward purchase and/or sale operations in that currency against dinars on the foreign exchange market.

The foreign exchange position is qualified as long when assets exceed commitments; it is qualified as short when commitments exceed assets.

Article 2: The overall foreign exchange position, all currencies combined, is equal to the sum of the dinar equivalent values of the foreign exchange positions per currency.

Article 3: Positions in foreign currencies resulting from the settlement of foreign exchange transactions may only be held on the foreign currency money market.

TITLE II
PRUDENTIAL RULES FOR THE MONITORING OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE POSITIONS

Article 4: The rate to be applied for calculating the dinar equivalent value of the foreign exchange position in a currency is the average of the bid and ask rates as displayed by the Central Bank of Tunisia on electronic information systems at 4 p.m.1.

Article 5: Each Approved Intermediary is required to permanently observe:

1°) A maximum ratio of 10% between the amount of the foreign exchange position in each currency and the amount of its net own funds.

2°) A maximum ratio of 20% between the amount of the overall foreign exchange position and the amount of its net own funds.

1 11 a.m. during the single trading session. Net own funds are determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of Circular N°91-24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 17, 1991, concerning The daily exchange result by currency is constituted by the difference between:

- the balance of the "exchange position" suspense account valued on the basis of the average of the buying and selling rates as displayed by the Central Bank of Tunisia on the electronic information systems at 4 p.m.,

- and the balance of the "countervalue of the exchange position" account.

TITLE IV
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

Article 9: Authorized Intermediaries are required to make available to the Central Bank of Tunisia statements conforming to the models provided in the annexes, detailing the exchange position by currency throughout the day and the overall exchange position, all currencies combined, at the end of the day.

Article 10: All provisions contrary to or duplicating the present circular, and in particular circular n° 94-02 of February 1, 1994, are hereby repealed.
